summary: Create a new draft course
criteria: Given I am an authenticated Academic Admin with Create permission, When I POST /api/v1/courses with courseCode, courseName, courseType, duration, totalCredits, departmentId, description, prerequisites and tags, Then a new course document is persisted with status=DRAFT and version="1.0", And a CourseCreated event is published, And the response returns id, courseCode, status, version and createdAt per the sample Create Course Response (Panel 6/7, FR-01).

summary: Enforce scoped course-code uniqueness
criteria: Given a courseCode already exists within the institution, When a create or code-change request is submitted with the same normalized code, Then the request is rejected with a 409 Conflict error per the Failure Handling table, and no document is written (BR-01, Panel 11/12).

summary: Normalize course code before validation
criteria: Given a courseCode is submitted in any casing or with leading/trailing whitespace, When the create/update request is processed, Then the service normalizes the code prior to running the uniqueness check (BR-02).

summary: Update a draft course
criteria: Given a course is in status=DRAFT and I hold Update permission, When I PUT /api/v1/courses/{id} with changed fields, Then the fields are updated in place and version metadata is incremented, And attempting the same update once the course is ACTIVE requires the governed new-version path instead (API Design Panel 3, Key Business Rules Panel 11).

summary: Validate department reference on course create/update
criteria: Given a departmentId is supplied on create or update, When the service validates it against course_departments/Department reference data, Then the request succeeds only if the department exists and is active, otherwise a 400 Invalid department error is returned (Failure Handling Panel 12).

summary: Enforce total credits greater than zero
criteria: Given a course draft has totalCredits <= 0, When a submit-for-approval or publish action is attempted, Then the action is rejected with a validation error, consistent with the rule 'Total credits must be greater than zero' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

summary: View course detail
criteria: Given a valid course id and an authenticated user with view permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/courses/{id} is called, Then the current course document is returned with HTTP 200, scoped per the RBAC matrix in Panel 8.

summary: Retrieve course credit information
criteria: Given a course exists, When GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/credits is called, Then totalCredits and any credit breakdown are returned, sourced from the course and course_evaluation_policy collections (API Design Panel 3).

summary: Support bulk import and export of course records
criteria: Given a properly formatted bulk import file, When it is submitted via the bulk import endpoint, Then each row is validated against the same business rules as a single create (uniqueness, department, credits), row-level errors are reported without aborting the whole batch, and a bulk export produces an equivalent file of current course records (Responsibilities Panel 2).

summary: Search and filter courses
criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/courses/search with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then matching results are returned using indexed queries within the performance target, and only fields appropriate to my role are included (API Design Panel 3, FR-09).

summary: Retrieve the published course catalog
criteria: Given one or more courses have been published to the catalog, When GET /api/v1/courses/catalog is called, Then only catalog-projected, published-course entries are returned from course_catalog, excluding DRAFT/REVIEW/deactivated courses (API Design Panel 3).

summary: Maintain the course_catalog projection on publish/update
criteria: Given a course transitions status or its published fields change, When the change commits, Then the course_catalog document is synchronously or eventually updated to match, and a CourseCatalogUpdated event is emitted (MongoDB Collections Panel 4, Events Panel 9).

summary: Restrict catalog visibility for students to active/published courses
criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Student, When I search or browse the catalog, Then only ACTIVE, catalog-visible courses are returned regardless of query filters, per the Student role's 'View published course catalog' permission (RBAC Panel 8).

summary: Create a new version on material change
criteria: Given a course has a currently ACTIVE/published version, When I submit a material change, Then a new course_versions document is created with an incremented version number and its own effectiveFrom date while the current version remains immutable, And a CourseVersionCreated event is emitted (BR-06, BR-13, Events Panel 9).

summary: Publish a course version
criteria: Given a version has passed validation, When I call POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/publish, Then the version's status becomes effective, the course status moves toward ACTIVE, the prior version is superseded, and a CourseVersionCreated/CoursePublished event pair is emitted per Panel 9 (API Design Panel 3).

summary: Enforce non-overlapping effective dates across versions
criteria: Given an existing version is effective for a date range, When a new version is submitted with an overlapping effective date range, Then the request is rejected with a validation error, consistent with the rule 'Effective date must not overlap with existing version' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

summary: Require a new version for changes to a published course
criteria: Given a course's current version is ACTIVE, When a caller attempts to directly mutate published fields instead of creating a new version, Then the operation is rejected, consistent with 'Changes to published course require new version' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

summary: Retrieve version history for a course
criteria: Given a course with one or more versions, When I call GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/versions, Then all versions are returned ordered by version number with status and effective dates (API Design Panel 3).

summary: Prevent mutation of published versions
criteria: Given a course_versions document has status=effective/published, When any update operation targets that document directly, Then the operation is rejected at the application and repository layer (BR-06).

summary: Add a course prerequisite
criteria: Given both the source and prerequisite courses exist and are valid, When I POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/prerequisites with prerequisiteCourseId, type and mandatory flag, Then the relationship is validated for cycles and persisted, and a CoursePrerequisiteAdded event is emitted (API Design Panel 3, Events Panel 9).

summary: Reject prerequisite cycles
criteria: Given adding a proposed prerequisite edge would create a cycle in the directed prerequisite graph, When the add-prerequisite request is validated, Then the request is rejected and 'Prerequisites must be valid and active courses' is enforced (Key Business Rules Panel 11, BR-10).

summary: Reject prerequisites referencing an invalid or inactive course
criteria: Given a prerequisiteCourseId does not resolve to an active course, When the add-prerequisite request is validated, Then it is rejected with a 404 Not Found error per the Failure Handling table (Panel 12).

summary: Remove a course prerequisite
criteria: Given an active prerequisite relationship exists, When I call DELETE /api/v1/courses/{id}/prerequisites/{prerequisiteId}, Then the relationship is removed/deactivated and a CoursePrerequisiteRemoved event is emitted (API Design Panel 3, Events Panel 9).

summary: List prerequisites for a course
criteria: Given a course id, When I call GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/prerequisites, Then all active prerequisite relationships are returned via an indexed lookup.

summary: Associate a course with its owning department
criteria: Given a course is created or its department changes, When the association is written, Then a course_departments document links courseId to departmentId with an effective date, matching the diagram's 'Department association' purpose (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

summary: Reassign a course to a different department
criteria: Given a course currently belongs to Department A, When an authorized user reassigns it to Department B, Then a new course_departments record is created effective from the reassignment date while the prior association is retained for history, and only authorized roles (Registrar/Department Head with cross-department permission) may perform this action (RBAC Panel 8).

summary: List all courses owned by a department
criteria: Given I am a Department Head, When I query courses scoped to my department, Then only courses associated with my departmentId in course_departments are returned, consistent with the 'Manage department courses' permission (RBAC Panel 8).

summary: Record accreditation details for a course
criteria: Given a course requires regulatory accreditation, When I submit accreditation details (authority, reference, validFrom/validTo), Then a course_accreditation document is created and linked to the course, matching 'Accreditation & regulatory details' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

summary: Enforce mandatory accreditation for regulatory course categories
criteria: Given a course is classified as a regulatory category, When a publish action is attempted without an associated valid course_accreditation record, Then publication is blocked with a validation error, consistent with 'Accreditation details mandatory for regulatory courses' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

summary: Alert on expiring accreditation
criteria: Given a course_accreditation record's validTo date is within the configured lead-time window, When the monitoring check runs, Then a notification is raised to the accountable Academic Admin/Department Head.

summary: Link a course to its curriculum reference
criteria: Given a course is linked to a curriculum defined in ACD-02, When the mapping is created or updated, Then a course_curriculum_map document records the reference by identifier only, consistent with 'Provide course structure' (Cross-Module Integration Panel 10).

summary: Map subjects to a course
criteria: Given ACD-03 publishes or the admin records subject-to-course associations, When the mapping is synchronized, Then course_subjects reflects the current subject set for the course, matching 'Map subjects to course' (Cross-Module Integration Panel 10, MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

summary: Expose course structure to Curriculum and Subject modules via API/events
criteria: Given ACD-02/ACD-03 need course structural context, When they call the relevant REST endpoints or consume ACD-01's domain events, Then they receive course/curriculum/subject linkage data consistent with the Cross-Module Integration table (Panel 10), and never query ACD-01's database directly.

summary: Record a course-batch offering
criteria: Given a batch defined in ACD-04 offers a course, When the offering is recorded, Then a course_batch_offerings document links courseId, batchId and the offering term, matching 'Batch-wise course offerings' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

summary: Block course deactivation while active batch offerings exist
criteria: Given a course has one or more active entries in course_batch_offerings, When a deactivate action is attempted, Then it is rejected with a validation error, consistent with 'Course deactivation allowed only if no active batches' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

summary: List batch offerings for a course
criteria: Given a course id, When I query its batch offerings, Then all current and historical course_batch_offerings entries are returned, indexed by courseId.

summary: Define an attendance policy for a course
criteria: Given a course requires a specific attendance rule, When I submit a minimum attendance percentage and any exceptions, Then a course_attendance_policy document is created/updated and linked to the course, matching 'Attendance rules per course' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

summary: Define an evaluation/credit policy for a course
criteria: Given a course's evaluation structure is being defined, When I submit component weightages (internal/external) and credit distribution, Then a course_evaluation_policy document is created/updated and the total resolves to the course's totalCredits, matching 'Evaluation/credit rules' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4, Key Business Rules Panel 11).

summary: Expose attendance and evaluation policy to ACD-06/EXM via API
criteria: Given ACD-06 or EXM needs a course's policy, When they call the relevant read endpoint, Then the current effective attendance/evaluation policy is returned, versioned consistently with the course's current version.

summary: Attach a document to a course
criteria: Given a document has been uploaded to the platform's document/object storage, When I link it to a course, Then a course_documents record is created referencing the document by identifier/URL, document type and version, matching 'Brochures, regulations, syllabi' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4). Actual file bytes are never embedded in MongoDB.

summary: List and retrieve documents for a course
criteria: Given a course has one or more linked documents, When I query them, Then metadata (title, type, version, link) is returned, filtered by my role's visibility (public brochure vs internal regulation).

summary: Replace or version a course document
criteria: Given a document already exists for a course, When I upload a replacement, Then a new course_documents version entry is created and marked current, while the prior entry is retained for audit.

summary: Add tags/keywords to a course
criteria: Given a course exists, When I add one or more tags (e.g. "UG", "APPLICATIONS"), Then a course_tags document is created/updated linking the tags to the course, matching the sample Create Course Request's tags array (Panel 7, MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

summary: Search courses by tag/keyword
criteria: Given courses have been tagged, When I search using a tag filter, Then matching courses are returned via an index on course_tags.

summary: Archive a retired course into course_archive
criteria: Given a course transitions to an archived/retired status, When the archive action completes, Then a course_archive record is created (or the course is soft-deleted and flagged) with a reference back to its final version and history, matching 'Archived/retired courses' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4) and 'Soft delete - retain for audit and reporting' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

summary: Query archived/retired courses for audit and reporting
criteria: Given I hold the Auditor role, When I query course_archive, Then all archived/retired course records are returned with their final state and links to course_history, consistent with the Auditor's 'View course history and changes' permission (RBAC Panel 8).

summary: Update course lifecycle status
criteria: Given a requested status transition, When I call PUT /api/v1/courses/{id}/status, Then the transition is validated against the allowed state machine, the status is updated, and the change is recorded in course_history (API Design Panel 3).

summary: Reject invalid lifecycle transitions
criteria: Given a requested transition is not permitted from the course's current status, When the transition action is invoked, Then the request is rejected with a 400 Business rule violation error per the Failure Handling table, and the course status remains unchanged (Panel 12).

summary: Retrieve change history for a course
criteria: Given a course has one or more history entries, When I call GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/history, Then all course_history entries are returned in chronological order with actor and timestamp (API Design Panel 3, RBAC Panel 8).

summary: Publish the full ACD-01 domain event catalog via transactional outbox
criteria: Given a course create/update/activate/deactivate/version/prerequisite/catalog operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event from the Events catalog (Panel 9) is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged.

summary: Notify stakeholders on course creation
criteria: Given a course is created, When the CourseCreated event is published, Then the Notification Service sends the configured stakeholder notification, matching Step 6 of the Create Course sequence diagram (Panel 6).

summary: Deduplicate inbound events using event identity
criteria: Given an inbound event has already been processed successfully, When it is redelivered, Then the service recognizes the duplicate and skips reprocessing without error.

summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue
criteria: Given an inbound or outbound event fails processing after the maximum configured retry attempts, When retries are exhausted, Then the event is persisted to dead_letter_events with failure context and an alert is raised, consistent with 'Event publishing failure -> retry with backoff' then store-in-outbox/retry-async (Failure Handling Panel 12).

summary: Guarantee exactly-once processing of retried academic commands
criteria: Given an idempotencyKey and operation, when the same key is replayed with an identical request hash, then the original responseRef is returned without reapplying the operation | Given the same idempotencyKey is replayed with a mismatched request hash, then the request is rejected as a conflicting duplicate | Given expiresAt passes, then the idempotency record is eligible for cleanup without affecting already-completed operations (MongoDB Collections Panel 4, Reliability Panel 12).

summary: Enforce the full 7-role RBAC permission matrix
criteria: Given a user attempts an action without the corresponding permission for their role, When the request reaches the service, Then it is rejected with a 401/403 error per the Failure Handling table before any business logic executes, and the full matrix in RBAC Panel 8 is enforced consistently across every endpoint in the API Design panel.

summary: Grant Auditor read-only access to course history and changes
criteria: Given I hold the Auditor role, When I access any course_history, course_versions or course_archive endpoint, Then I receive read-only results and any write attempt is rejected, matching 'View course history and changes' (RBAC Panel 8).

summary: Grant External API consumers scoped read-only access
criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call any ACD-01 endpoint, Then I receive only the data within my granted scope and read-only access, matching 'Read-only access (as per scope)' (RBAC Panel 8).

summary: Record an immutable, append-only history entry for every material change
criteria: Given any material mutation occurs (create, update, submit, publish, activate, deactivate, prerequisite change, catalog update), When the mutation commits, Then a corresponding course_history record is written capturing action, actorId and timestamp, and history records can never be updated or deleted (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

summary: Attribute every material mutation to an authenticated actor
criteria: Given any material mutation request, When it is processed, Then the actorId from the authenticated identity token is persisted alongside the change (matching "createdBy": "admin123" in the sample response, Panel 7).

summary: Reject unauthorized and forbidden requests with the correct error codes
criteria: Given a request is unauthenticated or authenticated but lacking permission, When it is processed, Then it returns 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden respectively, exactly as documented in the Failure Handling table (Panel 12).

summary: Publish and version the ACD-01 API contract
criteria: Given the ACD-01 service, When the API contract is published, Then it documents all endpoints listed in the API Design panel (Panel 3) with methods, paths and descriptions, and breaking changes require a new version.

summary: Return standardized success and error response shapes
criteria: Given any ACD-01 API call, When the response is returned, Then it conforms to the sample Create Course Response envelope shown in Panel 7.

summary: Map every documented failure scenario to its specified error code
criteria: Given each documented failure condition occurs, When the API responds, Then it returns exactly the status defined in the Failure Handling table (Panel 12): 409 duplicate code, 400 invalid department, 404 prerequisite not found, 400 business rule violation, 500 database error, retry-with-backoff for event publishing failure, 401 unauthorized, 403 forbidden, 503 service unavailable.

summary: E2E: Create → Validate → Persist → Notify (full sequence)
criteria: Given a course creation request from the Admin Portal, When it flows through the API Gateway, ACD-01's validate/authorize/apply-business-rules/save steps, and the resulting event/notification fan-out, Then the response matches the documented 201 Created success response, and the Notification Service is confirmed to have sent the stakeholder notification (Sequence Diagram Panel 6).

summary: E2E: verify each cross-module integration contract
criteria: Given the ACD-01 release candidate, When the full integration suite runs against ACD-02, ACD-03, ACD-04, ACD-05, STM, EXM, HRM, COM and ACD-10 Reporting, Then every REST + Events integration listed in Panel 10 is validated, and this gate is required before the service is marked production-ready.

summary: E2E: deactivation blocked by active batches, then succeeds after batch closure
criteria: Given a course has an active course_batch_offerings entry, When deactivation is attempted, then rejected, and then re-attempted after the batch offering is closed, Then the first attempt fails per the business rule and the second succeeds with status updated and history recorded.

summary: Create a new draft curriculum
criteria: Given I am an authenticated Academic Admin with CURRICULUM_CREATE permission, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula with courseId, academicPattern, academicYear, departmentId, campusId and name, Then a new curricula document is persisted with status=DRAFT and a first curriculum_versions document at version=1, And a CurriculumCreated event is written to the outbox, And the response returns curriculumId, version and status per the Standard Response envelope (FR-01, UC-01).

summary: Validate courseId resolves through ACD-01
criteria: Given a courseId is supplied on create, When the service validates it against ACD-01's course reference API, Then the request succeeds only if the course exists and is active, otherwise ACD2_COURSE_INVALID (422) is returned and no document is written (BR-05, Exceptions §15).

summary: Enforce tenant/campus/department scope consistency
criteria: Given a curriculum references a course or subject from a different tenant/campus scope, When the request is validated, Then it is rejected with a 403/422 tenant-mismatch error, consistent with BR-13 and the Exceptions table's 'Tenant mismatch' scenario.

summary: View curriculum detail
criteria: Given a valid curriculumId and a user with CURRICULUM_VIEW permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id} is called, Then the current curriculum document (with its effective version reference) is returned with HTTP 200 (UC-11).

summary: Enforce read-only access for the Student Portal
criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Student, When I access curriculum data via the Student Portal, Then only PUBLISHED/effective curriculum content is returned and it is strictly read-only, consistent with the Student Portal (Read Only) channel shown in the architecture diagram.

summary: Search and filter curricula
criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/academics/curricula with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then results are returned within the P95 <500 ms indexed-read target, and only fields appropriate to my role/classification are included (FR-14, NFR §16).

summary: List active curricula
criteria: Given one or more curricula have a PUBLISHED/EFFECTIVE version, When I call GET /api/v1/active (or the equivalent filtered list endpoint), Then only curricula with an effective version are returned (API Design panel, diagram endpoint list).

summary: Create a new curriculum version for an academic period
criteria: Given a curriculum exists, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions with effectiveFrom/effectiveTo and regulation details, Then a new curriculum_versions document is created in DRAFT status, and a CurriculumVersionCreated event is emitted (FR-02, UC-02, Sequence Diagram panel 6).

summary: Update a draft curriculum version
criteria: Given a curriculum_versions document is in status=DRAFT, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v} with changed fields, Then the draft is updated in place, And attempting the same update once the version is PUBLISHED is rejected with ACD2_VERSION_IMMUTABLE (409) (FR-03, BR-02, Exceptions §15).

summary: Enforce exactly one effective version per course/academic period
criteria: Given a course/academic-period pair already has an effective published version, When another version for the same course/academic period is published, Then the prior version is atomically superseded within the same transaction, and any attempt to publish an overlapping effective period without superseding is rejected with a 409 conflict (BR-01, Exceptions §15 'Overlapping effective periods').

summary: Prevent mutation of published versions
criteria: Given a curriculum_versions document has status=PUBLISHED, When any update operation targets that document directly, Then the operation is rejected with ACD2_VERSION_IMMUTABLE (409) and no field is altered (BR-02, BR-12).

summary: Retrieve version history for a curriculum
criteria: Given a curriculumId with one or more versions, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions, Then all versions are returned ordered by version number with status and effective dates.

summary: Retrieve a specific historical curriculum version
criteria: Given a curriculumId and a version number that exists, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}, Then the immutable snapshot for that version is returned unchanged from when it was published (BR-12).

summary: Clone the effective version into a new draft for annual revision
criteria: Given a curriculum has a currently effective version, When I initiate an annual revision, Then a new draft version is created pre-populated with the effective version's semesters, subjects, syllabus, credits and outcomes, ready for edits, per Workflow 14.2 (Annual Revision).

summary: Reject stale writes with optimistic version locking
criteria: Given a client submits an update based on a stale version reference, When the write is attempted, Then it is rejected with ACD2_VERSION_CONFLICT (409) instructing the client to reload the latest version (Exceptions §15 'Stale version').

summary: Add a semester to a curriculum version
criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=DRAFT, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/semesters with semesterNo, name and academicYear, Then a semester entry is added to the version (UC-03, Domain Model panel 5).

summary: Enforce unique semester sequence numbers within a version
criteria: Given a semesterNo already exists within the target curriculum version, When another semester is added with the same number, Then the request is rejected with a validation error (BR-07).

summary: Map a subject to a semester
criteria: Given a semester exists in the curriculum version, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/subjects with subjectId, semesterNo, subjectOrder, subjectType, credits, contactHours and mandatory, Then the subject reference is validated against ACD-03, a curriculum_subjects mapping is persisted, and a CurriculumSubjectMapped event is emitted (FR-04, BR-06, UC-04, sample Map Subject Request §29.2).

summary: Validate subjectId resolves through ACD-03
criteria: Given a subjectId is supplied on a mapping request, When the service validates it against ACD-03's subject reference API, Then the request succeeds only if the subject is active, otherwise ACD2_SUBJECT_INVALID (422) is returned and no mapping is persisted (BR-03, BR-06).

summary: Prevent duplicate subject-to-semester mapping
criteria: Given a subject is already mapped to a semester in the target version, When a duplicate mapping is submitted without an applicable repeat/elective policy exception, Then the request is rejected with ACD2_DUPLICATE_MAPPING (409) (BR-08).

summary: Remove a subject-to-semester mapping
criteria: Given a mapping exists in a DRAFT version, When I call DELETE /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/subjects/{mappingId}, Then the mapping is removed and a CurriculumSubjectUnmapped event is emitted (API Design §28, Event Contracts §31).

summary: Flag mappings when a referenced subject is deactivated
criteria: Given a SubjectDeactivated event is received for a subjectId referenced by one or more mappings, When the event is processed, Then affected mappings are flagged and any pending publication referencing them is blocked, consistent with 'Flag affected mappings; block publication if invalid' (Event Consumption §32).

summary: Define syllabus structure for a curriculum version
criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=DRAFT, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/syllabus with the module/topic structure, Then the syllabus structure is persisted against the version and a CurriculumSyllabusUpdated event is emitted (FR-05, UC-05, Event Contracts §31).

summary: Retrieve syllabus structure for a version
criteria: Given a curriculum version has a defined syllabus, When GET /api/v1/curricula/{id}/syllabus is called, Then the current syllabus structure for that version is returned (API Design panel, diagram endpoint list).

summary: Validate credit totals against configured academic policy
criteria: Given a curriculum version's aggregated subject credits are computed, When a submit-for-approval or publish action is attempted and the total violates configured policy (min/max), Then the action is rejected with ACD2_CREDIT_POLICY (422) detailing the violation (BR-09, Exceptions §15 'Credit policy violation').

summary: Add a learning outcome reference to a curriculum version
criteria: Given a curriculum version exists, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/outcomes with code, description, bloomLevel and type (CO/PO), Then a curriculum_outcomes document is persisted and a CurriculumOutcomeUpdated event is emitted (FR-06, Domain Model panel 5, Event Contracts §31).

summary: List learning outcomes for a curriculum version
criteria: Given a curriculum version has mapped outcomes, When GET /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/outcomes is called, Then all outcome references for that version are returned (API Design §28).

summary: Add a curriculum prerequisite
criteria: Given both curricula referenced in the relationship exist and are valid, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/prerequisites, Then the relationship is validated for cycles and persisted, and a CurriculumPrerequisiteUpdated event is emitted (FR-07, Event Contracts §31).

summary: Reject curriculum prerequisite cycles
criteria: Given adding a proposed prerequisite edge would create a cycle, When the add-prerequisite request is validated, Then it is rejected with ACD2_PREREQUISITE_CYCLE (422) and no edge is persisted (BR-10, Exceptions §15).

summary: List prerequisites for a curriculum
criteria: Given a curriculumId, When I query its prerequisites, Then all active prerequisite relationships are returned via an indexed lookup.

summary: Submit a draft curriculum version for approval
criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=DRAFT and passes structural validation, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/submit, Then the status transitions to REVIEW, a CurriculumSubmitted event is emitted, and the approval workflow is initiated (FR-08, UC-06, Curriculum Lifecycle §13).

summary: Department Head or Curriculum Committee reviews a submitted curriculum
criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=REVIEW and belongs to my department/committee scope, When I record my review decision, Then the decision is captured and, on rejection, the version returns to DRAFT/REVISION per the lifecycle diagram (UC-07, Curriculum Lifecycle §13).

summary: Approve a reviewed curriculum version
criteria: Given a curriculum version has completed review, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/approve, Then the status transitions to APPROVED and a CurriculumApproved event is emitted (UC-08, RBAC §48).

summary: Publish an approved curriculum version
criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=APPROVED and all publication invariants (BR-14) are satisfied, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/publish, Then the version becomes effective, any prior effective version is superseded, and a CurriculumPublished event is emitted to ACD-01/03, EXM, LMS and Analytics (FR-09, UC-09, Workflow §14.1).

summary: Block publication until approval and structural validation are complete
criteria: Given a curriculum version lacks approval or fails any mandatory validation (invalid subject, credit policy, duplicate mapping, prerequisite cycle), When a publish action is attempted, Then it is blocked with ACD2_PUBLICATION_BLOCKED (409) identifying the failing condition, and no partial publish state is possible (BR-04, BR-14, Exceptions §15 'Approval missing').

summary: Retire a curriculum or version
criteria: Given a curriculum version is SUPERSEDED or otherwise eligible for retirement, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/retire, Then the status transitions to RETIRED, a CurriculumRetired event is emitted, and no data is deleted (FR-10, UC-10, Curriculum Lifecycle §13).

summary: Prevent deletion of curricula with downstream academic references
criteria: Given a curriculum has one or more downstream academic references, When a delete request is attempted instead of retirement, Then the request is rejected, consistent with BR-15's 'retirement is used instead' rule.

summary: Automatically supersede the prior version on publish
criteria: Given a curriculum has a currently effective version, When a new version is published, Then the prior version's status is atomically updated to SUPERSEDED in the same MongoDB transaction as the publish (Workflow §14.2, Transaction Strategy §56).

summary: Publish domain events via transactional outbox
criteria: Given a curriculum create/version/mapping/workflow operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event from the Event Contracts catalog (§31) is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged (Event Architecture §30).

summary: Emit CurriculumPublished to all downstream consumers

summary: Consume CourseDeactivated/CourseArchived and flag affected curricula

summary: Deduplicate inbound events using eventId

summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue

summary: Support idempotent create-version, mapping and lifecycle requests

summary: Use MongoDB transactions for coupled curriculum writes

summary: Grant the Accreditation Team read-only access for compliance and audit

summary: Apply bounded retry with exponential backoff for transient failures

summary: Enforce institution-scoped subject-code uniqueness

summary: Require a subject to be associated with a department

criteria: Given I hold SUBJECT_EDIT permission scoped to the subject's department, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id} with changed fields, Then the master fields are updated with optimistic concurrency enforced, and a SubjectUpdated event is emitted (UC-04, BR-12).

summary: Prevent hard deletion of a referenced or in-use subject
criteria: Given a subject is referenced in curriculum or has active batch offerings, When a hard-delete request is attempted, Then it is rejected with a 409 Conflict, consistent with 'Cannot delete subject if used in curriculum or active batches' (Key Business Rules panel 12, BR-05, Exceptions §15).

summary: Validate subject type against configured taxonomy
criteria: Given a subjectType is submitted that is not part of the configured taxonomy, When the create/update request is validated, Then it is rejected with a 422 validation error, consistent with 'Invalid subject type' (Exceptions §15, BR-04).

summary: Classify a subject as Theory, Practical, Tutorial, Project, Elective or Audit
criteria: Given a classification value is submitted, When it matches one of the configured categories (Subject Types & Categories panel 5 of the diagram: TH, PR, TU, PJ, EL, AU), Then the subject is classified accordingly and the value is retained for search/filter (FR-05).

summary: Validate credits and contact hours against institutional policy
criteria: Given credits or contactHours violate the configured policy for the subject's type/programme, When a create, update or publish action is attempted, Then it is rejected with a 422 validation error, consistent with 'Credit range and subject type must be valid for program' (Key Business Rules panel 12, BR-02, BR-03).

summary: Mark a subject as elective
criteria: Given the elective flag is submitted on create/update, Then the subject's elective indicator is persisted and returned in subsequent reads (Domain Model panel 6, sample request §29.1).

summary: Search and filter subjects
criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/search with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then results are returned within the P95 <2 sec target using indexed queries, and only fields appropriate to my role/classification are included (FR-09, Monitoring §52).

summary: Retrieve the published subject catalog
criteria: Given one or more subjects are ACTIVE and catalog-visible, When GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/catalog is called, Then only published/active subjects are returned, excluding DRAFT/DEPRECATED/RETIRED subjects (API Design panel 3, RBAC 'View published subjects (read-only)').

summary: List subjects by category or department
criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/subjects/category/{category} or /api/v1/subjects/department/{deptId}, When the request is processed, Then all matching active subjects are returned via an indexed lookup (API Design panel 3 of the diagram).

summary: Create a new subject version
criteria: Given a subject exists, When I POST /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions, Then a new subject_versions document is created in DRAFT status with the next monotonic version number, and a SubjectVersionCreated event is emitted (FR-06, UC-05, BR-10).

summary: Update a draft subject version
criteria: Given a subject_versions document is in status=DRAFT, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions/{v} with changed fields, Then the draft is updated in place, and attempting the same update once the version is PUBLISHED is rejected with a 409 immutable-resource error (FR-07, BR-06, Exceptions §15).

summary: Publish a subject version
criteria: Given a version has passed validation, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions/{v}/publish, Then the version's status becomes PUBLISHED, the prior published version is marked SUPERSEDED, and SubjectVersionPublished + SubjectVersionSuperseded events are emitted (UC-06, Event Contracts §31).

summary: Prevent mutation of published versions
criteria: Given a subject_versions document has status=PUBLISHED, When any update operation targets that document directly, Then the operation is rejected at the application and repository layer (BR-06, 'Published subjects are immutable (use versioning)' — Key Business Rules panel 12).

summary: Enforce monotonic, never-reused version numbers
criteria: Given a subject already has one or more versions, When a new version is created, Then it is assigned the next sequential number, and no prior version number can ever be reassigned (BR-10).

criteria: Given a subjectId with one or more versions, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions, Then all versions are returned ordered by version number with status and effective dates.

summary: Retrieve a specific historical subject version
criteria: Given a subjectId and a version number that exists, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions/{v}, Then the immutable snapshot for that version is returned unchanged from when it was published (BR-06).

summary: Reject stale writes with optimistic version locking
criteria: Given a client submits an update based on a stale version reference, When the write is attempted, Then it is rejected with a 409 optimistic-concurrency error instructing the client to reload the latest version (BR-12, Exceptions §15 'Stale version').

summary: Add or update extended metadata for a subject
criteria: Given a subject exists, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/metadata with the metadata fields, Then a subject_metadata document is created/updated (one per subject, enforced by a unique tenantId+subjectId index), and regulatory fields require elevated permission to set (Field-Level Data Dictionary §39, Validation Rules).

summary: Retrieve extended metadata for a subject
criteria: Given a subject has metadata recorded, When GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/metadata is called, Then the metadata document is returned, with L3 fields (regulatoryCode, prerequisiteNotes) filtered per the requester's classification clearance.

summary: Search subjects by metadata tag
criteria: Given subjects have been tagged via subject_metadata, When I search using a tag filter, Then matching subjects are returned via the multikey tenantId+tags index (Indexes §39).

summary: Add a subject prerequisite or co-requisite
criteria: Given both subjects exist, belong to the same permitted scope, and subjectId does not equal prerequisiteSubjectId, When I POST /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/prerequisites with prerequisiteSubjectId, relationshipType, mandatory and minimumGrade, Then the relationship is validated for cycles and persisted, and a SubjectPrerequisiteAdded event is emitted (subject_prerequisites §39, Event Contracts §31).

criteria: Given adding a proposed prerequisite edge would create a cycle in the directed prerequisite graph, When the add-prerequisite request is validated, Then it is rejected with a 409 error, consistent with 'No circular prerequisite dependencies' (Key Business Rules panel 12, Failure Handling panel 13).

summary: Prevent duplicate active prerequisite relationships
criteria: Given an active prerequisite relationship already exists between subjectId and prerequisiteSubjectId, When the same relationship is submitted again, Then it is rejected, consistent with 'Duplicate active relationships are prohibited' (Integrity/Consistency Rules §39).

summary: Block deactivated subjects from being newly introduced as prerequisites
criteria: Given prerequisiteSubjectId refers to a deactivated subject, When an add-prerequisite request is submitted without an explicit policy exception, Then it is rejected, consistent with 'deactivated subjects cannot be introduced as new prerequisites unless policy explicitly permits it' (Integrity/Consistency Rules §39).

summary: Remove a subject prerequisite
criteria: Given an active prerequisite relationship exists, When I call DELETE on the prerequisite resource, Then the relationship is deactivated/retired (not hard-deleted) and a SubjectPrerequisiteRemoved event is emitted, and historical relationships are retained for reconstruction (Retention/Lifecycle §39).

summary: List forward and reverse prerequisite dependencies for a subject

summary: Reactivate a subject

summary: Mark a subject as deprecated
criteria: Given a subject is ACTIVE, When a deprecate transition is invoked, Then the status transitions to DEPRECATED and a SubjectDeprecated event is emitted (Subject Lifecycle §13, Event Contracts §31).

summary: Retire a subject permanently
criteria: Given a subject is DEPRECATED or DEACTIVATED, When a retire transition is invoked, Then the status transitions to RETIRED and a SubjectRetired event is emitted, consistent with the version-lifecycle terminal state (Subject Lifecycle §13).

summary: Block new curriculum mapping of a deprecated/deactivated subject
criteria: Given a subject is DEPRECATED or DEACTIVATED, When ACD-02 attempts to map it as a new curriculum subject without an explicit policy exception, Then the reference validation call returns rejection, consistent with BR-11.

summary: Update controlled lifecycle status via a single governed endpoint
criteria: Given a requested status transition, When I call PUT /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/status, Then the transition is validated against the allowed lifecycle state machine, the status is updated, and the change is recorded in history (API Design §28, Activity — Subject Lifecycle §26).

summary: Retrieve change history for a subject
criteria: Given a subject has one or more history entries, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/history, Then all history entries are returned in chronological order with actor and timestamp (UC-09, API Design §28).

criteria: Given a batch is in status=DRAFT or OPEN and I hold BATCH_EDIT permission, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/batches/{id} with changed fields, Then the fields are updated with optimistic concurrency enforced, and a BatchUpdated event is emitted (API Design §28, BR-11).

summary: View batch detail
criteria: Given a valid batchId and a user with BATCH_VIEW permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/academics/batches/{id} is called, Then the current batch document is returned with HTTP 200, scoped per the RBAC matrix (UC-03, §49).

summary: Search and filter batches
criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/academics/batches/search or GET /api/v1/academics/batches with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then results are returned within the indexed-read performance target, and only fields appropriate to my role/classification are included (FR-13, UC-04).

summary: Restrict batch visibility for students to their own batch
criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Student, When I query batch data, Then only my own current batch/section context is returned, consistent with 'BATCH_VIEW for own/current academic batch context' (RBAC §49, Actors and Personas §8).

summary: Create a section within a batch
criteria: Given a batch exists, When I POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/sections with sectionCode, sectionName and capacity, Then a BatchSection sub-document is created within the batch aggregate, validated for a unique sectionCode within the batch (Domain Model §19, Class Model §20, sample Create Batch Request panel 8 of the diagram).

summary: List sections for a batch
criteria: Given a batch has one or more sections, When I call GET /api/v1/batches/{id}/sections, Then all section entries are returned with their capacity and status (API Design panel 3 of the diagram).

summary: Optionally assign faculty to a section
criteria: Given a section exists, When I assign a facultyId to it, Then the reference is stored by identifier only, consistent with 'Assign Faculty (Optional)' (Sample Workflow panel 14) and the Boundary Rule that ACD-04 stores only logical references.

summary: Enforce sections must have valid faculty assignment where required
criteria: Given institutional policy requires faculty assignment for section activation, When a section activation is attempted without a facultyId, Then it is rejected with a 422 validation error, consistent with 'Sections must have valid faculty assignment (if required)' (Key Business Rules panel 12 of the diagram).

summary: Set and update batch capacity
criteria: Given a batch exists, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/capacity with a new capacity value, Then the capacity is updated (must be positive unless zero-capacity planning drafts are explicitly permitted) and validated against the current roster count (FR-04, BR-03).

summary: Block roster additions that would exceed capacity
criteria: Given a batch's current roster count equals its capacity and no active override exists, When an add-student request is submitted, Then it is rejected with ACD_BATCH_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED (409), consistent with 'Total enrolled students cannot exceed batch capacity' (Key Business Rules panel 12, BR-04, sample Error Response §29.4).

summary: Grant an authorized capacity override
criteria: Given I hold CAPACITY_OVERRIDE permission with elevated approval, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/capacity-override with overrideCapacity, reason, approvedBy and effectiveFrom/To, Then a batch_capacity_overrides record is created with status=ACTIVE, a CapacityOverrideGranted event is emitted, and subsequent roster additions are permitted up to the override capacity (UC-07, Field-Level Data Dictionary §40).

summary: Expire or revoke a capacity override
criteria: Given an override's effectiveTo has passed or it is explicitly revoked, When a subsequent add-student request is evaluated, Then the override's status is EXPIRED/REVOKED and standard capacity enforcement applies again (batch_capacity_overrides §40, Indexes).

summary: Add a student to a batch roster
criteria: Given the batch is OPEN/ACTIVE and has available capacity (or an active override), When I POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/students with studentId, effectiveFrom and membershipType, Then the student's eligibility is validated via Student Management, a batch_rosters membership record is persisted, and a StudentAddedToBatch event is emitted (FR-05, UC-05, sample §29.2).

summary: Validate student eligibility before roster assignment
criteria: Given a studentId is supplied on an add-student request, When the service resolves and validates the student through Student Management, Then the request succeeds only if the student is found and eligible, otherwise it is rejected with a 422 validation error (BR-05, Exceptions §15 'Student not found/ineligible').

summary: Prevent duplicate active assignment to the same batch
criteria: Given a student is already actively enrolled in the target batch, When another add-student request is submitted for the same student, Then it is rejected/treated idempotently with a 409 conflict, consistent with BR-06 and Exceptions §15 'Student already assigned'.

summary: Remove a student from a batch roster
criteria: Given an active membership exists for the student in the batch, When I call DELETE /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/students/{studentId}, Then the membership status is ended (not hard-deleted), a StudentRemovedFromBatch event is emitted, and the historical membership record is retained (FR-07, UC-06, BR-09).

summary: Block new roster additions to a closed or archived batch
criteria: Given a batch is in status=CLOSED or ARCHIVED, When an add-student request is submitted, Then it is rejected with a 409 error, consistent with BR-07 and Exceptions §15 'Batch closed'.

summary: Retrieve the current roster for a batch
criteria: Given a batch exists, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/roster, Then all currently active membership records are returned (API Design §28).

summary: View point-in-time roster history
criteria: Given a batch has roster membership history recorded, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/history with a point-in-time parameter, Then the roster composition as of that date is reconstructed from batch_rosters and batch_history (UC-10 View Roster History).

summary: Open/activate a draft batch
criteria: Given a batch is in status=DRAFT and passes validation, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/open, Then the status transitions to OPEN then ACTIVE per policy, and BatchOpened/BatchActivated events are emitted (UC-01, UC-02, Workflow §14.1).

summary: Close a batch
criteria: Given a batch is ACTIVE and I hold closure authority, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/close, Then the status transitions to CLOSED, a BatchClosed event is emitted, new roster operations are blocked, and roster/history data is retained (FR-08, UC-08, Workflow §14.3).

summary: Reopen a closed batch
criteria: Given a batch is CLOSED and reopening is permitted by policy, When I call the reopen action, Then the status transitions back to ACTIVE and the transition is recorded in batch_history (UC-09, Batch Lifecycle §13).

summary: Archive a batch
criteria: Given a batch is CLOSED, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/archive, Then the status transitions to ARCHIVED, a BatchArchived event is emitted, and the record remains queryable for audit purposes (Sample Workflow panel 14 'Archive (for historical records)').

summary: Reject invalid lifecycle transitions
criteria: Given a requested transition is not permitted from the batch's current status per the defined state machine, When the transition action is invoked, Then the request is rejected with a 409/422 error and the batch status remains unchanged (Batch Lifecycle §13, Activity — Batch Lifecycle §26).

summary: Split a batch into multiple batches
criteria: Given a batch's enrollment justifies splitting, When Academic Admin calls POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/split with the target section definitions, Then the batch enters status=PENDING_SPLIT_APPROVAL and ACD-04 publishes a BatchSplitApprovalRequested payload (envelope: eventId, eventType, eventVersion=1.0, tenantId, institutionId, correlationId, timestamp) with data: { requestId, requestType:"SPLIT", sourceBatchId, sourceBatchCode, departmentId, campusId, requestedBy, requestedAt, reason, proposedSections:[{sectionCode, capacity, targetStudentIds[]}], approverRole:"REGISTRAR" }. The split is NOT executed at this point. On later receipt of a BatchSplitApprovalDecided event with decision=APPROVED (see 'Consume approval decisions...' story), new batches are created, affected roster memberships are reassigned with full history retained on both source and new batches, and a BatchSplit event is emitted. Split does not require cross-department sign-off since source and target batches stay within the same department by default.

summary: Merge two or more batches
criteria: Given multiple batches (potentially from different departments) are eligible for merging, When Academic Admin calls POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/merge with the source batch identifiers, Then the affected batches enter status=PENDING_MERGE_APPROVAL and ACD-04 publishes a BatchMergeApprovalRequested payload (same envelope) with data: { requestId, requestType:"MERGE", sourceBatchIds[], sourceBatchDepartmentIds[] (one per source batch, needed for the cross-department check), targetBatchId (null if a new batch is created), campusId, requestedBy, requestedAt, reason, approverRole:"REGISTRAR" }. The merge is NOT executed at this point. On later receipt of a BatchMergeApprovalDecided event with decision=APPROVED, rosters are consolidated into the target batch with history retained, the source batches are closed/archived, and a BatchMerged event is emitted.

summary: Consume ADM02's approval decision and execute or revert the split/merge
criteria: Given a batch is in status=PENDING_SPLIT_APPROVAL or PENDING_MERGE_APPROVAL, When ACD-04 consumes a BatchSplitApprovalDecided / BatchMergeApprovalDecided payload (same envelope) with data: { requestId, decision:"APPROVED"|"REJECTED", decidedBy, decidedAt, reason }. event matching that requestId, Then on decision=APPROVED the split/merge executes per its own story and a BatchSplitApproved/BatchMergeApproved event is emitted; on decision=REJECTED the batch reverts to its prior status, no roster changes occur, and the reason is recorded in batch_history. ACD-04 exposes NO local approve/reject endpoint of its own — the approval action itself happens inside ADM02's existing generic workflow engine (ADM02_workflow_instances), consistent with delegating approval rather than duplicating it.

summary: Publish domain events via transactional outbox
criteria: Given a batch create/roster/capacity/lifecycle operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event from the Event Contracts catalog (§31) is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged (Event Architecture §30 'Batch State + Roster + History + Outbox').

summary: Consume StudentCreated and StudentStatusChanged events
criteria: Given a StudentCreated or StudentStatusChanged event is received, When it is processed, Then a new student reference becomes available for future roster assignment, or affected memberships are flagged/blocked from future assignment respectively, without duplicating student personal master data (Event Consumption §33, Boundary Rule §3).

summary: Consume CourseUpdated and CourseDeactivated events
criteria: Given a CourseUpdated or CourseDeactivated event is received for a courseId referenced by one or more batches, When the event is processed, Then course reference context is refreshed, or affected batches are flagged/blocked according to policy without deleting their history (BR-14, Event Consumption §33).

summary: Consume CurriculumPublished and AcademicCalendarPublished events
criteria: Given a CurriculumPublished or AcademicCalendarPublished event is received, When it is processed, Then the relevant reference context on affected batches is refreshed where used (Event Consumption §33).

summary: Deduplicate inbound events using eventId
criteria: Given an inbound event with an eventId already processed successfully, When it is redelivered, Then the service recognizes the duplicate and skips reprocessing without error (Event Consumption §33).

summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue
criteria: Given an inbound or outbound event fails processing after the maximum configured retry attempts, When retries are exhausted, Then the event is persisted to dead_letter_events with failure context and an alert is raised (Retry Strategy §55, Monitoring §53).

summary: Support idempotent create, roster and lifecycle requests
criteria: Given a request is retried with the same idempotency key and identical payload, When it is reprocessed, Then the original result is returned without re-executing the write (FR-14, §56).

summary: Reject stale writes with optimistic version locking
criteria: Given a client submits an update based on a stale version, When the write is attempted, Then it is rejected with a 409 optimistic-concurrency error (BR-11, Exceptions §15 'Stale version').

summary: Use MongoDB transactions for coupled batch/roster writes
criteria: Given a create or add-student operation touches batches, batch_rosters, batch_history and outbox_events, When the operation executes, Then all writes commit atomically or none do (Transaction Strategy §57, Workflow §14.2 step 13).

summary: Enforce the full RBAC permission matrix
criteria: Given a user attempts an action without the corresponding permission for their role, When the request reaches the service, Then it is rejected with 401/403 per the Error Handling table (§54) before any business logic executes, and the full matrix in §49 (with its ABAC examples: tenant/institution scope match, department scope, capacity-override elevated permission) is enforced consistently across every endpoint.

summary: Grant Parent read-only access to their child's batch and section
criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Parent linked to a specific student, When I access batch/section data via the Parent Portal, Then I receive only my linked child's current batch and section context, strictly read-only, consistent with 'View child's batch and section' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Grant the Accreditation Team read-only access to batch history and reports
criteria: Given I am authenticated as Accreditation Team, When I access batch history or reporting endpoints, Then I receive read-only results, consistent with 'View batch history and reports' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Grant External API consumers scoped read-only access
criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call any ACD-04 endpoint, Then I receive only the data within my granted scope and read-only access, matching 'Read-only access (as per scope)' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Record an immutable, append-only history entry for every material change
criteria: Given any material mutation occurs (create, update, roster add/remove, capacity override, open, close, archive), When the mutation commits, Then a corresponding batch_history record is written capturing action, actorId, timestamp and before/after context, and history records can never be updated or deleted (Audit Model §47, 'Maintain complete audit trail of all batch changes' — Key Business Rules panel 12).

summary: Classify and protect batch data by sensitivity level
criteria: Given a field is classified L3 (membership source, notes, override approvals, audit) or L4 (outbox/idempotency/DLQ operational payloads), When a user without sufficient clearance queries batch data, Then those fields are excluded from the response (Data Classification §50). Student personal master data is never replicated into ACD-04 — only the minimum identifier needed for roster operations is stored.

summary: Encrypt batch and roster data at rest and in transit
criteria: Given ACD-04 is deployed to any environment, When traffic flows between clients, the API gateway and MongoDB, Then TLS is enforced end-to-end, encryption at rest is enabled, and no credentials or access tokens are ever stored in batch/roster documents (Encryption and Secrets §51).

summary: Emit structured logs with correlation context
criteria: Given any API call to ACD-04, When the request completes (success or failure), Then a structured log entry containing all required fields is emitted with no secrets/tokens present, and correlation/trace IDs propagate through asynchronous events (Logging and Observability §52).

summary: Expose operational metrics and distributed tracing
criteria: Given ACD-04 is running in production, When metrics are scraped and traces are sampled, Then all listed metrics are available on the monitoring dashboard and a trace can be followed across the full request path (§52).

summary: Alert on SLO-breaching and reliability signals, including roster reconciliation
criteria: Given any monitored signal crosses its defined threshold, When the breach is sustained beyond the alerting window, Then an alert fires to the on-call channel with enough context to begin triage, including the roster reconciliation check (Monitoring and Alerting §53).

summary: Apply bounded retry with exponential backoff for transient failures
criteria: Given a transient failure occurs on a retryable operation, When the retry policy executes, Then attempts back off exponentially with jitter up to a maximum bound, and deterministic validation failures are never retried (Retry Strategy §55).

summary: Meet indexed read/write performance targets
criteria: Given production-representative load, When each workload type is exercised, Then API P95 stays within the documented threshold and roster reads P95 stay under the documented target, verified in performance testing (Performance §60, MongoDB Index Strategy §44).

summary: Validate disaster recovery via regular restore tests
criteria: Given the configured backup schedule, When a scheduled restore test is executed against a non-production environment, Then the restored dataset is verified complete and consistent, including roster membership integrity (Disaster Recovery and Backup §58).

summary: Publish and version the ACD-04 API contract
criteria: Given the ACD-04 service, When the API contract is published, Then it documents every endpoint in the REST API Specification (§28) with request/response schemas, and breaking changes require a new API version.

summary: Return standardized success and error envelopes
criteria: Given any ACD-04 API call, When the response is returned, Then it conforms to the Standard Response / Error Response shapes in §29.3/29.4.

summary: Map every documented failure family to its specified HTTP status
criteria: Given each documented failure condition occurs, When the API responds, Then it returns exactly the status defined in the Error Handling table (§54): 400 malformed, 401 authentication, 403 authorization, 404 not found, 409 conflict (duplicate/student-already-assigned/stale-version/capacity), 422 validation (course/semester/eligibility), 429 rate limit, 500 internal, 503 dependency unavailable.

summary: E2E: Create → Sections → Faculty (optional) → Activate → Enroll → Monitor Capacity
criteria: Given a fresh batch is created via UC-01, When it proceeds through section definition, optional faculty assignment, activation and student enrollment, Then roster count and capacity are consistent at every step and the resulting events (BatchCreated, BatchActivated, StudentAddedToBatch) are observed, verified end-to-end (Sample Workflow panel 14 of the architecture diagram).

summary: E2E: capacity override enables enrollment beyond default capacity, then expires
criteria: Given a batch is at its configured capacity, When an add-student is rejected, a capacity override is granted, the add-student then succeeds, and the override subsequently expires, Then a further add-student attempt beyond the original capacity is rejected again, verified end-to-end.

summary: E2E: batch closure blocks new enrollment while preserving roster history
criteria: Given an ACTIVE batch with existing roster members, When Workflow §14.3 (Close Batch) is executed end-to-end, Then the batch status becomes CLOSED, a further add-student attempt is rejected with 409, and all prior roster/history entries remain intact and queryable (Workflow §14.3, BR-07/08/09).

summary: Validate integrations with ACD-01, ACD-02, ACD-03, ACD-05, ACD-06, STM, HRM, EXM, COM and ACD-10 before production sign-off
criteria: Given the ACD-04 release candidate, When the full integration suite runs against ACD-01 (validate course & program), ACD-02 (validate semester structure), ACD-03 (ensure subject availability), ACD-05 (allocate timetable slots), STM (student enrollment & validation), HRM (faculty assignment), EXM (batch-wise exam scheduling), COM (notify batch-related updates) and ACD-10 (batch analytics & reports), Then all contract, event-schema and E2E scenarios pass, and this gate is required before the service is marked production-ready (Production Definition of Done §69, Cross-Module Integration panel 11).

summary: Define BATCH_SPLIT_APPROVE / BATCH_MERGE_APPROVE permission codes and grant them to Registrar
criteria: Given the new permission codes are registered in the platform's central role→permission catalog (owned by the College Admin Module's Identity/Role & Access capability, not by ACD-04 itself), When the Registrar role is provisioned, Then BATCH_SPLIT_APPROVE and BATCH_MERGE_APPROVE are included in its grant set by default, and no other role (including Academic Admin and Department Head) holds either permission unless a future explicit decision changes this. This decision (Registrar, not Department Head, chosen specifically because merges can span batches from more than one department and Registrar's authority is not department-scoped) is not documented in either the ACD-04 DDD or the architecture diagram and should be captured in both.

summary: Define BATCH_SPLIT_REQUEST permission for Academic Admin
criteria: Given Academic Admin holds BATCH_SPLIT_REQUEST but not BATCH_SPLIT_APPROVE/BATCH_MERGE_APPROVE, When they call the split or merge endpoint, Then the request-initiation succeeds and enters a pending-approval state, but any attempt by that same actor to call the approve/reject endpoint on their own request is rejected with 403, enforcing separation of duties between requester and approver.

summary: Carry a full roster-reassignment map in BatchSplit/BatchMerged events for downstream reconciliation
criteria: Given a split or merge executes after Registrar approval, When the BatchSplit or BatchMerged event is published, Then its payload includes: sourceBatchId(s), resultingBatchId(s), and a per-student array mapping each affected studentId from its old batchId/sectionId to its new batchId/sectionId. Given this event schema, When ACD-05, STM, HRM, EXM or ACD-10 consume it, Then each can update its own batch-scoped records without a follow-up query to ACD-04. NOTE: this story defines what ACD-04 must publish; it does NOT define how ACD-05/STM/HRM/EXM/ACD-10 consume and apply it — those are gaps in THEIR respective DDDs (none of which were available when this backlog was built) and should be raised as action items with each module's owning team before batch split/merge ships.

summary: Create a new timetable draft
criteria: Given I am an authenticated Academic Admin with TIMETABLE_CREATE permission, When I POST /api/v1/academics/timetables with timetableCode, name, academicYear, semester, departmentId, programId and effectiveFrom/To, Then a new timetables document is persisted with status=DRAFT and currentVersion="v1", And a TimetableCreated event is written to the outbox, And the response returns timetableId, status and version per the Standard Response envelope (FR-01, UC-01, sample §30).

summary: Update draft timetable metadata
criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT and I hold TIMETABLE_EDIT permission, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id} with changed metadata, Then the fields are updated with optimistic concurrency enforced, and attempting the same update on a PUBLISHED timetable is rejected with 409 (BR-05, BR-10, Exceptions §16 'Stale draft').

summary: View timetable detail
criteria: Given a valid timetableId and a user with TIMETABLE_VIEW permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id} is called, Then the current timetable document (with its current version reference) is returned with HTTP 200 (§29).

summary: Delete a draft timetable
criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT and has never had a published version, When I call DELETE /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}, Then it is soft-deleted, and attempting the same on a timetable with any PUBLISHED/SUPERSEDED version history is rejected with 409 (API Design §29).

summary: Search and filter timetables
criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then results are returned within the search P95 <2sec indexed target, and only fields appropriate to my role/classification are included (FR-11, NFR §17).

summary: View the published timetable for a batch
criteria: Given a batch has a currently effective published timetable version, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/batch/{batchId}, Then only the effective, published schedule is returned, never a DRAFT/VALIDATING version (UC 'View Batch Timetable', API Design §29).

summary: View the assigned timetable for a faculty member
criteria: Given I am authenticated as Faculty, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/faculty/{facultyId} for my own facultyId, Then only my assigned, published entries are returned, consistent with 'VIEW assigned timetable' (RBAC §50).

summary: View room utilization
criteria: Given a room has published timetable entries, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/room/{roomId}, Then the room's full published schedule is returned, consistent with 'View room utilization' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

summary: View department-level timetable
criteria: Given I am a Department Head, When I call GET /api/v1/departments/{id}/timetable, Then all published timetables scoped to my department are returned, consistent with 'Manage department timetable' (RBAC panel 9, API Design panel 3 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Export a timetable
criteria: Given I hold TIMETABLE_EXPORT permission, When I call GET /api/v1/export for a given timetableId/scope, Then a PDF/Excel export is produced consistent with my role's field visibility, and a TimetableExported event is emitted (API Design panel 3, Events panel 10 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Add a slot entry to a draft timetable
criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT, When I POST /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/entries with batchId, subjectId, facultyId, roomId, dayOfWeek, period and entryType, Then a timetable_entries document is created within the draft and a TimetableEntryAdded event is emitted (FR-02, UC 'Add Entry', sample §30).

summary: Classify an entry by session type
criteria: Given an entryType value is submitted, When it matches one of the configured categories (Timetable Entry Types panel 5 of the architecture diagram: TH, PR, LAB, TU, SEM, EVT, EXM), Then the entry is classified accordingly and the value is retained for search/filter and conflict-rule selection (Class Model §21).

summary: Update a draft entry
criteria: Given an entry exists in a DRAFT timetable, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/entries/{entryId} with changed fields, Then the entry is updated and a TimetableEntryUpdated event is emitted, and the same operation on a PUBLISHED timetable is rejected with 409 (BR-05, Sequence — Add/Update Entry §23).

summary: Remove a draft entry
criteria: Given an entry exists in a DRAFT timetable, When I call DELETE /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/entries/{entryId}, Then the entry is removed and a TimetableEntryRemoved event is emitted (API Design panel 3, Events panel 10 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Support bulk entry creation from a weekly template
criteria: Given a set of entries is submitted together against a DRAFT timetable, When the bulk create request is processed, Then each entry is validated individually, row-level errors are reported without aborting the whole batch, and successfully created entries are persisted, consistent with 'Support recurring schedules (weekly templates)' (Responsibilities panel 2 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Validate batch, subject, faculty and room references on entry creation
criteria: Given an entry is submitted with batchId, subjectId, facultyId and roomId, When the service validates each reference against its owning service, Then the request succeeds only if all references exist and are active, otherwise it is rejected with 422 (Invalid subject/faculty/batch) and publication is blocked, consistent with BR-04 and Exceptions §16.

summary: Reject cross-tenant references
criteria: Given a referenced resource belongs to a different tenantId than the timetable, When the reference is validated, Then the request is rejected, consistent with BR-09 'Cross-tenant references are prohibited'.

summary: Refresh reference context on upstream reference updates
criteria: Given a BatchUpdated or SubjectUpdated event is received for a referenced entity, When it is processed, Then the local reference-validation cache/context is refreshed and any DRAFT timetable referencing that entity is flagged for re-validation (Events Consumed §33).

summary: Run conflict detection on a draft timetable
criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT with one or more entries, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/validate, Then the conflict engine checks faculty, room, batch, subject-policy, calendar, availability and duplicate-entry conflicts per the Conflict Model (§15), persists conflict_results, and the timetable transitions to VALIDATING then VALIDATED or INVALID, and a TimetableValidated event is emitted (FR-04, FR-10, UC-Validate, Sequence — Validate §24).

summary: Detect faculty double-booking
criteria: Given two entries share the same tenant+facultyId+day+period within overlapping effective scope, When conflict detection runs, Then a BLOCKING conflict of type FACULTY is recorded, consistent with BR-01 and the sample error 'Faculty FAC-100 is double-booked in MONDAY P2' (Error Contract §54).

summary: Detect room double-booking
criteria: Given two entries share the same tenant+roomId+day+period within overlapping effective scope, When conflict detection runs, Then a BLOCKING conflict of type ROOM is recorded, consistent with BR-02.

summary: Detect batch double-booking
criteria: Given two entries share the same tenant+batchId+day+period within overlapping effective scope, When conflict detection runs, Then a BLOCKING conflict of type BATCH is recorded, consistent with BR-03.

summary: Detect duplicate entries
criteria: Given two entries within the same timetable share an identical timetable+slot+subject/batch key, When conflict detection runs, Then a conflict of type DUPLICATE_ENTRY is recorded (Conflict Model §15).

summary: Detect calendar and faculty/room availability conflicts
criteria: Given an entry's date/period falls outside the published academic calendar, or outside a faculty/room's availability window, When conflict detection runs, Then a conflict of type CALENDAR or AVAILABILITY is recorded respectively, consistent with the Conflict Model (§15) and BR-07.

summary: Revalidate on FacultyAvailabilityChanged
criteria: Given a FacultyAvailabilityChanged event is received for a facultyId referenced by one or more timetables, When the event is processed, Then affected draft/operational timetables are flagged and re-validation is triggered, consistent with 'Revalidate affected draft/operational timetable' (Events Consumed §33).

summary: Retrieve conflict diagnostics for a timetable
criteria: Given a timetable has recorded conflict_results, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/conflicts, Then all conflicts are returned with type, severity, involved entry IDs and a human-readable message (FR-10, API Design §29).

summary: Guarantee conflict results are reproducible
criteria: Given a historical timetable version and its reference context at the time of validation, When the conflict engine is re-run against that exact input, Then it produces the identical conflict_results set, consistent with BR-11.

summary: Publish a validated timetable
criteria: Given a timetable is in status=VALIDATED with zero blocking conflicts, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/publish, Then a new immutable timetable_versions document is frozen and marked PUBLISHED, any prior effective version for the same scope is marked SUPERSEDED atomically, and a TimetablePublished event is emitted (FR-06, BR-05, BR-12, Sequence — Publish §25).

summary: Block publication of an unvalidated or conflicting timetable
criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT/INVALID or has one or more BLOCKING conflicts, When a publish action is attempted, Then it is rejected with 422 and publication is blocked, consistent with FR-06, BR-06 and the sample error contract (§54).

summary: Enforce publication effective-from date against the academic calendar
criteria: Given an effectiveFrom date is submitted for publication, When it falls outside the academic calendar policy window (per ACD-07's published calendar), Then publication is rejected with 422, consistent with FR-08 and BR-07.

summary: Prevent mutation of published versions
criteria: Given a timetable_versions document has status=PUBLISHED, When any update operation targets that document or its entries directly, Then the operation is rejected, consistent with FR-07 and BR-05 'Published versions are immutable'.
