summary: Clone the effective version into a new draft for changes
criteria: Given a timetable has a currently effective published version, When I initiate a change, Then a new draft version is created pre-populated with the effective version's entries, ready for edits, per the Change Workflow (§14.2).

summary: Supersede the prior version on republication
criteria: Given a timetable has a currently effective version, When a new version is published for the same scope, Then the prior version's status is atomically updated to SUPERSEDED and TimetableSuperseded/TimetableChanged events are emitted, while downstream propagation remains asynchronous (BR-08, BR-12, Sequence — Supersede §26).

summary: Retrieve version history for a timetable
criteria: Given a timetableId with one or more versions, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/versions, Then all versions are returned ordered by version number with status and effective dates (API Design §29).

summary: Reject stale writes with optimistic version locking
criteria: Given a client submits an update based on a stale version reference, When the write is attempted, Then it is rejected with 409 optimistic-concurrency error, consistent with BR-10 and Exceptions §16 'Stale draft'.

summary: Validate faculty lab rights for Laboratory entries
criteria: Given an entry has entryType=LAB (Laboratory), When the facultyId is validated, Then the request checks a lab-rights/qualification flag on the faculty reference (source and exact field not specified in the ACD-05 DDD — needs confirmation with HRM/Faculty domain ownership) and is rejected if absent, consistent with 'Lab sessions must be assigned faculty with lab rights' (Key Business Rules panel 12 of the architecture diagram). NOTE: not specified in the DDD; the source of truth for 'lab rights' must be confirmed with architecture before implementation.

summary: Create an ad-hoc/one-off session without disrupting the published schedule
criteria: Given an ad-hoc session is proposed for a specific date/period, When it is validated against the currently published schedule for the same batch/faculty/room, Then it is rejected if it would violate any existing published entry, consistent with 'Ad-hoc sessions must not violate existing schedules' (Key Business Rules panel 12 of the architecture diagram). NOTE: not specified in the ACD-05 DDD as a distinct entity/workflow from a normal timetable entry — whether ad-hoc sessions get their own lifecycle/collection or reuse timetable_entries with a flag needs architectural confirmation.

summary: Support recurring weekly templates for standard session types
criteria: Given a weekly template is defined for a batch/course combination, When a new term's draft timetable is created from that template, Then the standard recurring entries are pre-populated, consistent with 'Support recurring schedules (weekly templates)' (Responsibilities panel 2 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Publish domain events via transactional outbox
criteria: Given a timetable/entry/validation/publication operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction ('Timetable + Version + Conflict + Outbox', Event Architecture §31) and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged.

summary: Emit TimetablePublished to all downstream consumers
criteria: Given a timetable version is published, When the TimetablePublished event is emitted, Then it includes eventId, entityId, correlationId, timetableVersion, effectiveFrom and status per the Event Contract schema (§34), and all listed downstream consumers can deserialize and apply it.

summary: Consume BatchCreated, BatchUpdated and SubjectUpdated reference events
criteria: Given a BatchCreated, BatchUpdated or SubjectUpdated event is received, When it is processed, Then reference context for new/changed entities is refreshed, and any affected draft timetable's validation context is refreshed accordingly (Events Consumed §33).

summary: Consume AcademicCalendarPublished and revalidate impacted schedules
criteria: Given an AcademicCalendarPublished event is received, When it is processed, Then affected timetables are flagged and revalidated against the new calendar, consistent with 'Validate effective dates and impacted schedules' (Events Consumed §33).

summary: Deduplicate inbound events using eventId
criteria: Given an inbound event with an eventId already processed successfully, When it is redelivered, Then the service recognizes the duplicate and skips reprocessing without error.

summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue
criteria: Given an inbound or outbound event fails processing after the maximum configured retry attempts, When retries are exhausted, Then the event is persisted to dead_letter_events with failure context and an alert is raised, consistent with 'Downstream unavailable -> Asynchronous retry/DLQ' (Exceptions §16, Retry Strategy §56).

summary: Support idempotent create, entry and publish requests
criteria: Given a request is retried with the same idempotency key and identical payload, When it is reprocessed, Then the original result is returned without re-executing the write, consistent with 'Duplicate request -> Idempotent response' (Exceptions §16, Idempotency §57).

summary: Use MongoDB transactions for coupled timetable writes
criteria: Given a validate or publish operation touches timetables, timetable_versions, conflict_results and outbox_events, When the operation executes, Then all writes commit atomically or none do, consistent with 'Timetable + Version + Conflict + Outbox' (Event Architecture §31, Transaction Strategy §58).

summary: Enforce the full RBAC permission matrix
criteria: Given a user attempts an action without the corresponding permission for their role, When the request reaches the service, Then it is rejected with 401/403 per the HTTP Error Mapping (§55) before any business logic executes, and the full matrix in §50 is enforced consistently across every endpoint.

summary: Grant the Exam Cell scoped permission to manage exam timetables
criteria: Given I am authenticated as Exam Cell, When I create or update an entry with entryType=EXM, Then the action is permitted where policy allows, consistent with 'Manage exam timetables if applicable' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram); actions on non-exam entry types remain denied.

summary: Grant Facilities Manager read-only access to room utilization
criteria: Given I am authenticated as Facilities Manager, When I access room timetable/utilization endpoints, Then I receive read-only results across all rooms in my scope, consistent with 'View room utilization' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Grant External API consumers scoped read-only access
criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call any ACD-05 endpoint, Then I receive only the data within my granted scope and read-only access, matching 'Read-only access (as per scope)' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

summary: Record an immutable, append-only history entry for every material change
criteria: Given any material mutation or authorization failure occurs, When it is processed, Then a corresponding audit record is written capturing action, actorId and timestamp, and audit records can never be updated or deleted, consistent with FR-12 and the Audit Model (§48).

summary: Classify and protect timetable data by sensitivity level
criteria: Given a field is classified L3 (conflict diagnostics, actor/reason/audit) or L4 (outbox/idempotency/DLQ payloads), When a user without sufficient clearance queries timetable data, Then those fields are excluded from the response while L1 published-display fields remain visible per role (Data Classification §51).

summary: Minimize replicated personal data
criteria: Given a timetable entry references a faculty member, When the entry is persisted, Then only the facultyId reference is stored, with no name, contact, employment or personal data replicated, consistent with 'ACD-05 minimizes replicated personal data' (Data Classification §51).

summary: Emit structured logs with correlation context
criteria: Given any API call to ACD-05, When the request completes (success or failure), Then a structured log entry containing all required fields is emitted, and correlationId propagates through to any published events (Observability §52).

summary: Expose operational metrics and distributed tracing
criteria: Given ACD-05 is running in production, When metrics are scraped and traces are sampled, Then all listed metrics are available on the monitoring dashboard and a trace can be followed across the full request path (§52).

summary: Alert on conflict-rate spikes, validation latency, publish failures and stale drafts
criteria: Given any monitored signal crosses its defined threshold, When the breach is sustained beyond the alerting window, Then an alert fires to the on-call channel with enough context to begin triage (Monitoring and Alerts §53).

summary: Apply bounded retry with exponential backoff for transient failures
criteria: Given a transient failure occurs on a retryable operation, When the retry policy executes, Then attempts back off exponentially with jitter up to a maximum bound, and deterministic validation/conflict failures are never retried (Retry Strategy §56).

summary: Meet indexed read/write performance targets
criteria: Given production-representative load, When each workload type is exercised, Then normal API P95 <300ms, search P95 <2s and validation P95 <2s for a normal weekly timetable are met, verified in performance testing (NFR §17, Performance §61).

summary: Validate disaster recovery via regular restore tests
criteria: Given the configured backup schedule, When a scheduled restore test is executed against a non-production environment, Then the restored dataset is verified complete and consistent, including conflict_results reproducibility (Disaster Recovery §59).

summary: Publish and version the ACD-05 API contract
criteria: Given the ACD-05 service, When the API contract is published, Then it documents every endpoint in the REST API Specification (§29) with request/response schemas, and breaking changes require a new API version.

summary: Return standardized success and error envelopes
criteria: Given any ACD-05 API call, When the response is returned, Then it conforms to the Request/Response JSON (§30) and Error Contract (§54) shapes.

summary: Map every documented failure scenario to its specified HTTP status
criteria: Given each documented failure condition occurs, When the API responds, Then it returns exactly the status defined in the HTTP Error Mapping table (§55): 400 malformed, 401 unauthenticated, 403 scope/permission denied, 404 not found, 409 version/conflict state, 422 scheduling/reference validation failure, 429 rate limited, 500 unexpected, 503 dependency unavailable.

summary: E2E: Create Draft → Add Entries → Validate → Resolve Conflicts → Publish
criteria: Given a fresh timetable draft is created via UC-Create Draft, When entries are added, validation is run, blocking conflicts are corrected and the timetable is republished, Then it transitions DRAFT -> VALIDATING -> VALIDATED -> PUBLISHED, and the resulting TimetableCreated/TimetableValidated/TimetablePublished events are observed, verified end-to-end (Primary Workflow §14, Testing Strategy §69).

summary: E2E: mid-term change clones, revalidates and supersedes cleanly
criteria: Given a timetable has a currently effective published version, When the Change Workflow (§14.2) is executed end-to-end, Then the new version becomes effective, the prior version is marked SUPERSEDED and remains queryable, and TimetableChanged/TimetableSuperseded events are observed by ACD-06/LMS/CAM/EXM/Analytics consumers.

summary: E2E: publication blocked by an unresolved faculty conflict, then succeeds after correction
criteria: Given a draft timetable has two entries double-booking the same faculty member in the same slot, When validate is called (BLOCKING conflict recorded, publish rejected with 422) and then one entry is corrected and validate is re-run, Then the second validate returns zero blocking conflicts and the subsequent publish succeeds, verified end-to-end.

summary: Validate integrations with ACD-02, ACD-03, ACD-04, STM, HRM, SYS, EXM, COM and ACD-10 before production sign-off
criteria: Given the ACD-05 release candidate, When the full integration suite runs against ACD-02 (semester structure), ACD-03 (subject scope), ACD-04 (batch/enrollment context), STM (faculty details & availability), HRM (facility room details & capacity), SYS (academic events & holidays), EXM (exam timetables), COM (timetable update notifications) and ACD-10 (timetable analytics), Then all contract, event-schema and E2E scenarios pass, and this gate is required before the service is marked production-ready (Production Definition of Done §70, Cross-Module Integration panel 11).

summary: Create an attendance session from a timetable slot
criteria: Given I am authenticated Faculty within my assignment scope (or an Academic Admin), When I POST /api/v1/academics/attendance/sessions with batchId, subjectId, timetableEntryId, attendanceDate and periodNo, Then a session is persisted with status OPEN and the eligible roster resolved into rosterCount, an AttendanceSessionCreated event is written to the outbox, and the response returns sessionId, status, rosterCount, requestId and correlationId (FR-01, FR-03, DDD sections 19 and 23). NOTE: the representative event in DDD Appendix E shows data.status ACTIVE, which is not a state in the section 13 lifecycle (DRAFT, OPEN, SUBMITTED, LOCKED, CORRECTED, ARCHIVED, CANCELLED); align the event sample with the lifecycle.

summary: Validate the timetable slot and fail closed when the timetable is unavailable
criteria: Given a session request, When timetableEntryId, attendanceDate and periodNo are checked against the effective timetable via the TimetableReferenceClient, Then the session is created only if the slot is valid and effective, otherwise the request is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_INVALID_TIMETABLE (422). Given ACD-05 is unavailable, When a new session is requested, Then it fails closed (503 dependency unavailable) and no unvalidated session is created (FR-02, DDD sections 11 and 56).

summary: Reject duplicate sessions for the same batch, subject, date and period
criteria: Given a session already exists for the same tenantId+batchId+subjectId+attendanceDate+periodNo, When another create request arrives, Then it is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_DUPLICATE_SESSION (409), and two concurrent creates result in exactly one session because the unique compound index enforces the rule at the data layer (FR-05, DDD section 34).

summary: Update an open attendance session
criteria: Given a session is in status OPEN and I am authorized for its scope, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/attendance/sessions/{id} with the changed fields and the current version, Then the session is updated with optimistic concurrency, and once the session is LOCKED the same call is rejected because post-lock state is immutable (DDD sections 22 and 34).

summary: View and list attendance sessions
criteria: Given sessions exist, When I request a session by sessionId or list sessions with filters, Then results are role-scoped, paginated and served from tenant-aware indexes (batch/date, status/date) within the indexed-read P95 target. NOTE: the DDD REST catalog (section 22) lists only create, record, update, student view and report; the get-by-id and list endpoints appear only in the architecture diagram API panel and should be added to the approved contract.

summary: Cancel an attendance session without deleting evidence
criteria: Given a session was created in error, When an authorized user cancels it, Then the status becomes CANCELLED (terminal, void), the session and any records are retained for audit rather than hard-deleted, and summaries are recalculated excluding it (DDD section 13; diagram rule 'Soft delete - retain records for audit and reporting'). NOTE: CANCELLED exists in the DDD lifecycle, but no cancel endpoint is in the DDD catalog; the diagram shows DELETE /attendance/sessions/{id} (soft).

summary: Mark attendance for a session
criteria: Given an OPEN session and an expected roster, When I POST /api/v1/academics/attendance/sessions/{id}/records with records[] (studentId, status) and submittedBy, Then the submission is validated against the expected roster, all records and the session counts are persisted atomically, the summary is recalculated and shortage evaluated, an AttendanceMarked event is written to the outbox, and the response reports the counts (FR-04, FR-06, DDD sections 20, 24 and 65).

summary: Validate that every student belongs to the session's batch roster
criteria: Given a submission contains a studentId not in the resolved roster, When it is validated, Then the whole submission is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_STUDENT_NOT_IN_BATCH (422) and nothing is persisted (atomic per FR-06). Given the roster source is unavailable, Then unvalidated writes are rejected rather than accepted (DDD sections 11 and 56).

summary: Validate attendance status against the configured status catalog
criteria: Given a submitted status, When it is checked against the institution's configured status catalog, Then unknown codes are rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_INVALID_STATUS (422), and an optional statusReason is stored for special statuses (DDD sections 11 and 36). NOTE: the DDD defines P/A/L with L meaning Leave and per-session leaveCount, while the diagram domain model shows P/A/L/E and its sample response reports lateCount. The meaning of L (Leave vs Late) and of E must be fixed in the status catalog before build, and the catalog must state how each status counts toward attendance percentage.

summary: Prevent duplicate attendance records for a student in a session
criteria: Given a record already exists for tenantId+sessionId+studentId, When another mark is submitted for the same student, Then it is rejected with a 409 conflict and the change must go through the correction path instead (unique index tenant+session+student, DDD Appendix D; diagram rule 'No duplicate attendance for same student/session').

summary: Enforce the configured marking time window
criteria: Given a session has a start and end time, When attendance is submitted outside the configured marking window, Then it is rejected with a business-rule error unless the late-entry rule permits it. NOTE: 'Attendance allowed only within configured time window' appears only in the diagram Key Business Rules. The DDD has a SessionWindow (start < end) but no marking-window rule; the window length, its configuration source and the error code must be defined before implementation.

summary: Exclude holidays and academic events from attendance
criteria: Given the academic calendar marks a date as a holiday or event day, When a session is created or attendance marked for that date, Then the action is rejected or flagged per policy and excluded from percentage calculations (diagram rules 'Holidays and academic events exclude attendance' and 'Real-time validation with academic calendar'). NOTE: the DDD lists ACD-07 Calendar only 'where applicable' (section 61); confirm whether the calendar is a hard dependency and whether a calendar outage fails closed.

summary: Record capture source and actor on every attendance record
criteria: Given a record is persisted, When it is written, Then markedBy, markedAt, source (FACULTY, MOBILE, BULK, IMPORT or SYSTEM), recordVersion and schemaVersion are stored (DDD Appendix C). NOTE: no BIOMETRIC or RFID source value exists in the DDD; see the Bulk Import & Device Integration epic.

summary: Support very large rosters with partitioned attendance records
criteria: Given a roster below the configured bound, When attendance is stored, Then records are embedded with the session; Given a roster above the bound or high write concurrency, Then records are stored in the separate/partitioned representation while preserving the unique session+student rule and the same read contract (ADR-ACD06-002, DDD sections 32, 35 and 58). The bound value must be a configuration decision validated by load testing.

summary: Correct an attendance record with a mandatory reason
criteria: Given a marked session and a correction request with studentId, newStatus, reason and expectedVersion, When the policy check passes, Then the record is updated and an attendance_corrections entry is appended in the same transaction, the session moves to CORRECTED, the summary is recalculated, and an AttendanceCorrected event is emitted (FR-07, DDD sections 21, 25 and 66). NOTE: the DDD catalog has no dedicated correction endpoint (PUT sessions/{id} is the nearest); the diagram uses PUT /attendance/records/{id} and /attendance/corrections. The endpoint shape must be confirmed.

summary: Enforce correction authorization scope
criteria: Given a caller without correction rights for the session's scope, When a correction is attempted, Then it is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_CORRECTION_FORBIDDEN (403) and the attempt is audited (DDD sections 50, 51 and 56).

summary: Keep an immutable, append-only correction trail
criteria: Given a correction is applied, When the entry is written, Then it captures oldStatus, newStatus, reason, correctedBy, correctedAt, authorizationScope, previousVersion, newVersion and correlationId, can never be updated or deleted, is access-restricted, is retrievable by session and student, and is retained longer than operational data (DDD sections 37, 38 and 51; ADR-ACD06-003).

summary: Reject stale corrections using the expected version
criteria: Given expectedVersion does not match the current recordVersion, When the correction is submitted, Then it is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_VERSION_CONFLICT (409) and nothing changes (DDD sections 25 and 53; ADR-ACD06-006).

summary: Support configurable late-entry corrections
criteria: Given a configured late-entry period, When a Faculty member corrects within the period, Then the correction proceeds under the normal audited path; after the period it requires the higher authorization scope (diagram rule 'Support late entry corrections (configurable)'). NOTE: not defined in the DDD; the period, its configuration source and the role that can override are open decisions.

summary: Route corrections through an approval workflow (decision required)
criteria: Given the approval workflow is adopted, When a correction is requested, Then it is held as pending, AttendanceCorrectionRequested is emitted, and only on approval is the record changed and the correction appended, with AttendanceCorrectionApproved or AttendanceCorrectionRejected emitted and the rejection reason retained (diagram rule 'Corrections require approval (HOD/Admin)', API panel and events panel). NOTE: this conflicts with the DDD, where a correction is applied directly by an authorized actor with a mandatory reason. Three decisions are needed first: (1) does approval replace or supplement the direct path, (2) which role approves (the diagram says HOD/Admin), and (3) does the workflow run locally or through the College Admin Module's Approvals & Workflow capability, as was decided for ACD-04 split/merge. If routed through ADM02, a matching workflow-type story is needed in the ADM02 backlog.

summary: Submit an attendance session
criteria: Given a session is OPEN with attendance recorded, When I submit it, Then the status becomes SUBMITTED and the submission is audited (DDD sections 13 and 51). NOTE: the DDD does not say whether unmarked roster members block submission or default to a status; confirm the rule.

summary: Lock a submitted session
criteria: Given a session is SUBMITTED, When it is locked, Then the status becomes LOCKED, direct edits to the session and records are rejected, and only the correction path can change outcomes (DDD section 34 'immutable post-lock semantics'; audit of lock per section 51).

summary: Archive completed sessions
criteria: Given a session is LOCKED or CORRECTED and past its operational window, When it is archived, Then the status becomes ARCHIVED, the archive is audited, records stay retained under the retention policy, and summaries remain valid (DDD sections 13, 51 and 60).

summary: Reject invalid lifecycle transitions
criteria: Given a requested transition is not allowed from the current status (for example OPEN directly to LOCKED, or any change from CANCELLED), When it is invoked, Then it is rejected with a 409 state-conflict error and the status is unchanged. NOTE: the DDD error taxonomy (section 53) has no invalid-transition code; one must be added.

summary: Close sessions at end of day
criteria: Given a configured end-of-day cut-off, When it passes, Then remaining OPEN or SUBMITTED sessions are closed per policy, an AttendanceSessionClosed event is emitted and the action is audited (diagram workflow step 'Close Session (End of Day)' and events panel). NOTE: the DDD has the LOCKED state but no trigger or timing for it; the cut-off, grace period and whether close means SUBMITTED or LOCKED must be defined.

summary: Recalculate the summary on every accepted mark or correction
criteria: Given attendance is marked or corrected, When the change is accepted, Then the summary for tenantId+studentId+subjectId+termId is created or updated with totalSessions, presentCount, absentCount, leaveCount, attendancePercentage, calculatedAt and sourceVersion, with a unique index guaranteeing one summary per key (FR-08, DDD sections 39, 40 and 46).

summary: Calculate attendance percentage under the academic rules
criteria: Given accepted records for a student, subject and term, When the percentage is aggregated, Then it is derived from eligible sessions and Present outcomes, excluding cancelled sessions and excluded holiday or event days (DDD section 46; diagram rule 'Attendance percentage calculated as per academic rules'). NOTE: the DDD does not say whether Leave, Late or on-duty statuses count as present or are removed from the denominator; the rule must be specified per status.

summary: Rebuild summaries and reconcile drift
criteria: Given summaries are derived data, When a rebuild or the periodic reconciliation runs, Then each summary is recomputed from attendance_records, drift is corrected and reported, and shortage state is re-evaluated (DDD sections 40 and 47).

summary: Expose summary freshness and support asynchronous materialization at scale
criteria: Given high marking volume, When summary materialization is asynchronous, Then calculatedAt is exposed where permitted, reconciliation closes any gap, and marking latency targets are met (DDD sections 55 and 56).

summary: View attendance summaries by student, batch and subject
criteria: Given summaries exist, When I request a student, batch or subject summary, Then results are role-scoped and served from the student/date, batch/shortage and subject/percentage indexes (DDD section 40). NOTE: the DDD catalog exposes only the student view and the report endpoint; the diagram adds /summary, /summary/student, /summary/batch and /summary/subject.

summary: Evaluate shortage against the configured minimum threshold
criteria: Given a summary changes or reconciliation runs, When the ShortageRuleEngine evaluates it, Then shortageFlag and shortageThreshold are set from the configured minimum (FR-09, DDD sections 39 and 47).

summary: Emit AttendanceShortageDetected only on a false-to-true transition
criteria: Given shortageFlag was false, When an evaluation sets it true, Then exactly one AttendanceShortageDetected event is written to the outbox; repeated evaluations while the flag stays true emit nothing (DDD section 47). NOTE: the DDD publishes this event but it is absent from the diagram events panel; keep the DDD behaviour.

summary: Resolve the applicable threshold from its authoritative source
criteria: Given a threshold is needed for a student, subject and term, When it is resolved, Then it comes from the agreed policy source with a defined precedence between institutional default and course-level rule. NOTE: the DDD says thresholds are 'configured' with Shared Configuration as an upstream dependency (section 61), while the ACD-01 design owns per-course attendance rules in course_attendance_policy. Decide which is authoritative, whether course-level overrides institution-level, and how ACD-06 reads it.

summary: Query shortage lists for a batch
criteria: Given shortage flags are maintained, When I request a batch shortage list, Then results are returned from the batch+shortageFlag index, scoped to my authorization (DDD sections 40 and 45).

summary: View a student's attendance history
criteria: Given a student has attendance data, When GET /api/v1/academics/attendance/student/{studentId} is called, Then a paginated history is returned only where I am the student, the linked parent or an authorized admin, with summary freshness shown where allowed (DDD sections 22, 45 and 50).

summary: Generate paginated attendance reports
criteria: Given report filters, When GET /api/v1/academics/attendance/report is called, Then results are paginated, Faculty see only their scope while Admin sees the whole institution, and indexed reports meet P95 < 2 seconds (FR-12, DDD sections 50 and 57; diagram responsibility 'Generate daily, weekly, monthly attendance reports').

summary: Export attendance reports with export controls
criteria: Given I hold export permission, When I request an export, Then the file respects my role's field visibility and masking, the export is audited, and an AttendanceExported event is emitted (DDD sections 49 and 51; diagram export endpoint and events panel). NOTE: the export endpoint and event are diagram-only; the DDD requires export audit and controls but defines no endpoint.

summary: Run heavy reports asynchronously
criteria: Given a report exceeds the synchronous size threshold, When it is requested, Then it is processed as an asynchronous job and retrieved on completion, while normal API P95 stays under 300 ms (DDD section 58).

summary: Bulk import attendance from CSV or Excel
criteria: Given a well-formed CSV or Excel file and import permission, When I POST /api/v1/academics/attendance/import, Then each row passes the same session, roster and status validation as normal marking, rows are stored with source IMPORT or BULK, and the response reports per-row errors, returning 207 partial success where some rows fail (diagram Import endpoint, failure panel and rule 'Bulk import allowed only for authorized users'). NOTE: not in the DDD catalog. Also decide whether partial success is compatible with FR-06 atomic persistence (atomic per session versus per row).

summary: Ingest attendance from biometric and RFID devices
criteria: Given a registered device submits attendance through the API/SDK, When the event is received, Then it is authenticated, mapped to a student and to the correct timetable session, validated like manual marking and stored with a device source, and device-integration failures return 503 without losing buffered data (diagram Capture Modes, Integration and Failure panels). NOTE: absent from the DDD, whose source enum has no BIOMETRIC or RFID. Open decisions: device identity and enrolment, student mapping, offline buffering and replay, and duplicate handling versus manual marks.

summary: Provide attendance to the external LMS
criteria: Given attendance is marked or corrected, When the LMS needs it, Then it receives the data through published events (DDD downstream consumers, section 62). NOTE: the diagram shows a REST sync to an external LMS while the DDD treats LMS as an event consumer; confirm whether a REST pull or push endpoint is required at all.

summary: Publish attendance events via the transactional outbox
criteria: Given a create, mark, correction or shortage transition commits, When the transaction completes, Then the event is recorded in outbox_events with the canonical envelope (eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, entityType, entityId, version, correlationId, data), correlation and causation IDs are preserved, and a publisher retries until acknowledged (FR-10, DDD sections 30, 31 and 41). NOTE: the diagram lists further events (AttendanceUpdated, AttendanceCorrectionRequested/Approved/Rejected, AttendanceSummaryGenerated, AttendanceSessionClosed, AttendanceExported); these are emitted only if the matching features are adopted.

summary: Consume TimetablePublished to establish timetable context
criteria: Given a TimetablePublished event is received, When it is processed, Then the effective timetable context used by session validation is updated (DDD section 29).

summary: Consume TimetableChanged and TimetableSuperseded (alignment needed)
criteria: Given ACD-05 publishes a new effective version, When the corresponding event is received, Then new sessions validate against the new version while existing sessions keep their original timetableEntryId as history. NOTE: the DDD consumes only TimetablePublished, but ACD-05 also emits TimetableChanged and TimetableSuperseded for mid-term changes, and its design does not say whether TimetablePublished also fires for a new version. If it does not, ACD-06 would keep validating against the old timetable. Align the contract with ACD-05 before build.

summary: Consume StudentAddedToBatch to refresh roster context
criteria: Given StudentAddedToBatch is received, When it is processed, Then the roster context used for future sessions includes the student from the event's effective date and already-recorded sessions are not rewritten (DDD section 29). NOTE: the ACD-04 diagram names this event StudentEnrolledInBatch; the DDDs use StudentAddedToBatch.

summary: Consume StudentStatusChanged to update eligibility
criteria: Given StudentStatusChanged is received, When it is processed, Then future rosters reflect the new eligibility while historical attendance truth is preserved unchanged (DDD section 29).

summary: Deduplicate inbound events by eventId
criteria: Given an event with an already-processed eventId is redelivered, When it arrives, Then it is recognised and skipped without error (DDD section 31).

summary: Route poison events to a dead-letter queue with controlled replay
criteria: Given an event fails after the configured retries, When retries are exhausted, Then it is stored in dead_letter_events with failureCode, failureReason, attemptCount and timestamps, an alert is raised, and it can be replayed under control (DDD sections 43 and 56).

summary: Consume BatchSplit and BatchMerged to keep attendance continuity (dependency gap)
criteria: Given ACD-04 publishes BatchSplit or BatchMerged with a per-student old-to-new batch map, When it is processed, Then future sessions resolve rosters from the new batches, open sessions on affected batches are handled per policy, historical sessions and records keep their original batchId, and each student's summary continues under the same student+subject+term key with its batchId updated. NOTE: split/merge is itself unspecified in the ACD-04 DDD and this event is not in the ACD-06 DDD's consumed list; this story records the dependency and needs sign-off from both service owners.

summary: Support idempotent create, mark and correct requests
criteria: Given a request is retried with the same tenantId+idempotencyKey and the same request hash, When it is reprocessed, Then the stored response is returned without re-executing the write; the same key with a different hash is rejected as a conflict; records expire through the TTL on expiresAt (FR-11, DDD sections 42 and 54).

summary: Apply optimistic concurrency to sessions and records
criteria: Given a write is based on a stale session version or recordVersion, When it is applied, Then it is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_VERSION_CONFLICT (409) (DDD sections 34, 44 and 53).

summary: Commit session, records and outbox atomically
criteria: Given a mark or correction touches sessions, records, corrections and outbox_events, When it executes, Then all writes commit atomically where the topology supports transactions, otherwise the outbox pattern guarantees eventual publication; summary materialization may be transactional for bounded workloads or asynchronous with reconciliation (FR-06, DDD sections 44 and 55).

summary: Enforce the API authorization matrix
criteria: Given a caller, When a request arrives, Then Super Admin has all rights, Academic Admin administers within the institution, Faculty creates and marks within assignment, Student holds ATTENDANCE_VIEW_SELF, Parent holds ATTENDANCE_VIEW_LINKED_STUDENT, Management reads authorized aggregates, and anything else is rejected with 403 (DDD sections 48 and 50).

summary: Limit Faculty to their assigned batches and subjects
criteria: Given a Faculty caller, When they create or mark a session, Then the batch/subject assignment is verified and violations are rejected and audited (DDD section 48; diagram rule 'Faculty can mark attendance only for assigned subjects/batches'). NOTE: the DDD does not name the assignment source (the ACD-05 timetable entry's faculty, or HRM); confirm it.

summary: Let Students view only their own attendance
criteria: Given I hold ATTENDANCE_VIEW_SELF, When I request attendance, Then only my records and summaries are returned and any other studentId returns 403 (DDD sections 48 and 50).

summary: Let Parents view their linked student's attendance
criteria: Given I hold ATTENDANCE_VIEW_LINKED_STUDENT, When I request attendance, Then only students linked to me are returned, read-only, based on the linkage authority in Student Management, and nothing about other students is exposed (DDD section 50).

summary: Let Department Heads view department attendance
criteria: Given I am a Department Head, When I request attendance, Then results are limited to my department's batches and subjects (diagram RBAC panel). NOTE: this role is not in the DDD authorization matrix.

summary: Give the Exam Cell consolidated read access
criteria: Given I am Exam Cell, When I request consolidated reports, Then I receive read-only results within my scope (diagram RBAC panel). NOTE: this role is not in the DDD matrix and the intended use (for example exam eligibility) is unspecified.

summary: Give External API consumers scoped read-only access
criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call an attendance endpoint, Then only data within my granted scope is returned and any write is rejected (diagram RBAC panel). NOTE: not in the DDD matrix.

summary: Guarantee tenant isolation on every query
criteria: Given any request, When data is queried or written, Then tenantId scoping is applied through tenant-aware compound indexes, cross-tenant access is impossible, and this is proven by security tests before release (DDD sections 45, 49 and 68).

summary: Audit every material attendance event
criteria: Given any listed event occurs, When it is processed, Then an audit entry records actor, requestId, correlationId and timestamp, and for corrections the old value, new value and reason (DDD section 51).

summary: Classify, encrypt and protect attendance data
criteria: Given attendance data, When it is stored or transmitted, Then TLS 1.2+ is enforced, encryption at rest and encrypted backups are enabled, secrets are centrally managed, projections are restricted by role and exports are controlled (DDD section 49).

summary: Emit structured logs, metrics and traces
criteria: Given production traffic, When requests complete, Then logs, API latency and error metrics, DB metrics, outbox lag, broker and consumer lag, session and record volume and shortage counts are available and a trace spans Gateway to consumers (DDD section 52).

summary: Alert on reliability and drift signals
criteria: Given a monitored signal breaches its threshold for the alert window, When detected, Then an alert with triage context reaches the on-call channel (DDD sections 52 and 56).

summary: Define behaviour under dependency outages
criteria: Given each outage, Then a timetable outage fails closed for new sessions, a roster outage rejects unvalidated writes, a broker outage falls back to the outbox, summary lag exposes freshness, an unauthorized correction is rejected and audited, and a poison event is retried then sent to the DLQ (DDD section 56).

summary: Apply bounded exponential backoff to transient failures
criteria: Given a transient failure, When retried, Then backoff is exponential and bounded, and deterministic domain failures are never retried (DDD section 54).

summary: Meet latency and high-volume marking targets
criteria: Given production-representative load, When exercised, Then availability is at least 99.9 percent, normal API P95 is under 300 ms, indexed search and report P95 is under 2 seconds and create or update is under 500 ms excluding async consumers, verified by performance tests (DDD sections 57 and 67).

summary: Scale horizontally with tenant-aware partitioning
criteria: Given rising load, When autoscaling triggers, Then capacity grows without interruption, bulk writes stay bounded, events are partitioned by tenant and session, and Redis may cache stable reference data (DDD section 58).

summary: Recover from disaster with post-restore reconciliation
criteria: Given the backup schedule, When a restore drill runs, Then the data is complete, correction history is intact, the outbox is recovered and summaries are reconciled from records afterwards (DDD section 59).

summary: Enforce data retention rules
criteria: Given each data type, Then records follow institutional and legal retention with soft delete only, corrections and audit are long-lived, summaries remain for the reporting horizon and are rebuildable, outbox rows stay until published and DLQ rows through incident closure (DDD section 60; diagram rule 'Soft delete - retain records for audit and reporting').

summary: Publish and version the attendance API contract
criteria: Given the service, When the contract is published, Then it covers the DDD catalog (create session, record attendance, update session, student view, report) and breaking changes require a new version (DDD sections 22 and 68). NOTE: the diagram lists roughly eighteen endpoints (sessions list and get, cancel, mark, import, records, corrections, summaries, export); the approved contract must state which are in scope.

summary: Return the standard envelope with pagination, filtering and sorting
criteria: Given any call under /api/v1, When it returns, Then it uses the standard envelope with requestId and correlationId and supports standardized pagination, filtering and sorting (DDD section 26).

summary: Map every failure to its documented error code and status
criteria: Given each failure, Then the API returns ACD_ATTENDANCE_INVALID_TIMETABLE 422, ACD_ATTENDANCE_STUDENT_NOT_IN_BATCH 422, ACD_ATTENDANCE_INVALID_STATUS 422, ACD_ATTENDANCE_DUPLICATE_SESSION 409, ACD_ATTENDANCE_CORRECTION_FORBIDDEN 403, ACD_ATTENDANCE_VERSION_CONFLICT 409 and 503 for unavailable dependencies (DDD section 53). NOTE: the diagram Failure Handling panel uses 400 for validation errors where the DDD uses 422; follow the DDD unless the architecture board decides otherwise. The diagram's 207 partial success applies only if bulk import is adopted, and 'session closed' has no DDD code yet.

summary: Publish attendance facts to Analytics and downstream consumers
criteria: Given attendance is marked, corrected or summarised, When events are published, Then LMS, CAM, ACD-10, Notification and the reporting warehouse can consume them through versioned contracts without direct database access (DDD sections 62 and 63).

summary: Provide early shortage-risk and marking-anomaly signals
criteria: Given accumulated attendance history, When the analytics layer runs, Then it produces advisory indicators including correlation with timetable and calendar changes, clearly labelled as advisory (DDD section 64).

summary: Guarantee intelligence cannot silently mutate attendance truth
criteria: Given any intelligence component, When it proposes a change, Then it can only do so through the service's own validated APIs under a human-authorized correction, and any such action is audited (DDD section 64).

summary: E2E: create, mark, summarise, detect shortage, correct and report
criteria: Given a valid timetable slot and roster, When a session is created, attendance marked, the summary and shortage evaluated, a correction applied and a report generated, Then every step succeeds, the expected events are observed and the report matches the corrected data (DDD sections 65, 66 and 67).

summary: E2E: a correction preserves history and recomputes derived state
criteria: Given a marked session, When an authorized correction is applied, Then the previous value is retained in the correction trail, the summary and shortage flag are recalculated, a single shortage event is emitted on a new crossing, and a stale correction is rejected with 409 (DDD sections 47 and 66).

summary: E2E: rejection paths
criteria: Given each invalid input (unscheduled slot, student not in batch, unknown status, duplicate session, unauthorized correction, stale version), When submitted, Then the documented code and status are returned and nothing is persisted (DDD section 53).

summary: E2E: mid-term timetable change does not corrupt attendance
criteria: Given existing sessions and a superseded timetable, When ACD-05 publishes a replacement, Then new sessions use the new timetable, old sessions and summaries are unchanged, and the ACD-05 event contract is confirmed to reach ACD-06 (see the timetable-change consumption story).

summary: E2E: batch split or merge preserves each student's attendance continuity
criteria: Given a batch with sessions and summaries, When ACD-04 executes an approved split or merge, Then new sessions resolve the new rosters, history keeps its original batchId and each student's summary continues under the same key. NOTE: depends on the unspecified ACD-04 split/merge design.

summary: Validate integrations before production sign-off
criteria: Given the release candidate, When the suite runs against ACD-01 (course details), ACD-03 (subject existence), ACD-04 (batch and section), ACD-05 (timetable session validation), HRM (faculty details), STM (student details), the academic calendar, COM (notifications), ACD-10 (analytics), the LMS and any devices, Then all REST and event contracts pass, and the Production Definition of Done items (approved OpenAPI, tested rules, deployed validators and indexes, working outbox/idempotency/DLQ, reviewed RBAC, verified audit, dashboards and tracing, tested DR, met load targets, registered event contracts, passed tenant isolation) are met (DDD section 68).

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to create an academic-calendar draft for my campus and academic year so that I can configure the authoritative planning calendar.
criteria: Gateway authenticates and applies tenant/institution/campus/year scope; required name, calendarCode, timezone and year are validated; DRAFT is created once per idempotency key; response contains calendarId, version, requestId and correlationId.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want duplicate calendar creation to be prevented so that each calendar code remains unique within its institutional scope.
criteria: Enforce tenantId+institutionId+campusId+academicYear+calendarCode uniqueness; return conflict on duplicate; same idempotency key/replay returns original result; changed payload is rejected.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve a calendar by ID so that I can review its configuration and lifecycle state.
criteria: Return authorized calendar metadata, status, currentVersion, effective boundaries and policy configuration; deny cross-scope access.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to update a draft calendar so that I can complete its configuration before submission.
criteria: Only editable lifecycle states may be changed; updatedBy/updatedAt are captured; optimistic version checking prevents lost updates; published versions cannot be edited.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to cancel or deactivate an unsubmitted draft so that obsolete drafts are not accidentally processed.
criteria: Only permitted draft states can be cancelled; transition is audited; cancelled drafts cannot be submitted or published.

summary: As an authorized management user, I want to search and filter calendars so that I can review academic schedules efficiently.
criteria: Support pagination, filtering, sorting and tenant/scope restrictions; indexed queries are used where applicable.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a term or semester to a draft calendar so that instructional periods are defined.
criteria: Only scoped editors can add terms to DRAFT; termCode and sequenceNo are unique within calendar; dates are valid; instructional dates remain within term boundaries.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want term-date overlaps to be rejected so that the academic calendar is internally consistent.
criteria: Check proposed terms against existing indexed terms; reject impermissible overlap with ACD_CALENDAR_TERM_OVERLAP 422; persist nothing on failure.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to update a term in a draft calendar so that academic-period changes can be managed before publication.
criteria: Use optimistic version checking; validate boundaries and instructional dates; audit the change; published term versions remain immutable.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve term details so that I can inspect dates, sequence and lifecycle state.
criteria: Return term, calendar reference, dates, instructional dates, status and version within authorized scope.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to deactivate a draft term so that an obsolete term is not used in the calendar.
criteria: Only non-published terms can be deactivated; change is recorded; references from draft events are validated.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to declare a holiday so that downstream planning reflects a non-working academic day.
criteria: Validate HOLIDAY type, date boundary, eventCode and NON_WORKING impact; save against calendar; audit and reliably publish HolidayDeclared.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a working-day override so that special instructional or closure days are represented correctly.
criteria: Validate WORKING_DAY_OVERRIDE and WORKING/NON_WORKING/NO_IMPACT; apply configured precedence; audit and version the change.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to schedule an academic event so that institutional activities are represented in the authoritative calendar.
criteria: Validate type, title, dates, allDay, impact, optional termId and academic-year boundary; enforce unique eventCode; return eventId/version.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to list calendar events so that I can review events by date, type and term.
criteria: Support date-range, type and term filtering with tenant/calendar scope enforcement and indexed access.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve an event by ID so that I can inspect its complete definition.
criteria: Return eventCode, eventType, title, dates, allDay, workingDayImpact, category, status and version.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to update a draft event so that schedule changes can be incorporated before publication.
criteria: Validate date/type/term rules; use optimistic version checking; audit change; reject edits to published event versions.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to deactivate a draft event so that obsolete events are not used.
criteria: Use soft lifecycle transition for editable events; preserve published history; record audit entry.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to validate a draft before submission so that I can correct conflicts and missing configuration.
criteria: Validate academic-year boundaries, term overlap, instructional containment, event conflicts, working-day precedence and publish prerequisites; return actionable errors without mutation.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want event dates outside the academic-year boundary to be rejected unless policy allows an exception.
criteria: Reject invalid boundaries; permit only approved institutional-policy exceptions; return deterministic validation error.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want holiday and academic-event conflicts detected before publication so that the calendar is internally consistent.
criteria: Identify conflicts using configured rules; block or classify them for review; do not silently modify source data.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want calendar impact analysis for proposed changes so that downstream effects can be understood before publication.
criteria: Compare proposed version with current published version and classify affected dates/terms/events and downstream consumers; analysis is advisory.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to submit a validated calendar for approval so that it follows academic governance.
criteria: Only validated DRAFT can transition to SUBMITTED; scope is checked; reason, requestId and correlationId are recorded; workflow reference is stored.

summary: As a Registrar, I want to approve or reject a submitted calendar so that only reviewed schedules can become effective.
criteria: Only SUBMITTED calendars may be decided; Registrar authorization is enforced; decision/reason are append-only; rejected drafts cannot publish until permitted resubmission.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to resubmit a corrected rejected calendar so that it can re-enter the approval process.
criteria: Only permitted rejected/correctable drafts may be resubmitted; new validation is required; history retains previous rejection reason and new submission.

summary: As a Registrar, I want to publish an approved calendar version so that one effective calendar is available for the campus.
criteria: Validate approval context, expectedVersion and actor scope; ensure draft is complete; publish new version atomically.

summary: As a Registrar, I want publication to supersede the previous current calendar atomically so that consumers never see two current versions.
criteria: Transactionally mark previous current version SUPERSEDED, establish new PUBLISHED version, append history and create outbox records; concurrent race returns version conflict.

summary: As a Registrar, I want to create a new draft from a published calendar so that changes preserve the immutable published record.
criteria: Clone required calendar/term/event state into a new editable version; preserve source version reference; classify impact before approval.

summary: As a System Administrator, I want published versions to be immutable so that historical academic decisions remain trustworthy.
criteria: Published calendar/term/event records cannot be updated destructively; changes require a new draft/version; history remains append-only.

summary: As an authorized academic consumer, I want to retrieve the current effective calendar for a campus and academic year so that planning uses authoritative dates.
criteria: Return the single current PUBLISHED calendar and relevant terms/events for authorized scope; no direct DB access.

summary: As an Attendance service consumer, I want to resolve effective term and working-day status for a date so that attendance rules use the correct calendar context.
criteria: Resolve effective calendar version by operating date, then apply term, holiday and working-day override precedence.

summary: As an authorized academic consumer, I want upcoming events and holidays in a date range so that dependent services can plan activities.
criteria: Return effective events within requested range using indexed date queries and authorized scope.

summary: As a Registrar, I want to review immutable calendar history so that I can trace approvals, publications and supersessions.
criteria: History is append-only and contains action, status transition, actor, timestamp, reason, correlationId and approvalRef where applicable.

summary: As a Compliance Officer, I want significant calendar and access actions audited so that governance and investigations have complete evidence.
criteria: Audit create/edit/term/holiday/event/submission/approval/publication/supersession/export and authorization failures with actor, scope, old/new state, reason, requestId and correlationId.

summary: As an Auditor, I want history queries filtered by calendar, actor and time so that investigations can be performed efficiently.
criteria: Support calendarId+changedAt and changedBy+changedAt access patterns while respecting governance permissions.

summary: As a Security Administrator, I want API Gateway authentication and trusted identity propagation so that only authenticated callers reach ACD-07.
criteria: Gateway authenticates caller, validates credential/token according to platform IAM, propagates trusted tenant/user context and rejects unauthenticated traffic.

summary: As a Security Administrator, I want RBAC and ABAC enforced so that calendar actions are restricted by role and academic scope.
criteria: Academic Admin can create/edit/submit in scope; Registrar can approve/publish/supersede; Management has authorized read; tenant/institution/campus/year predicates are enforced.

summary: As a Platform Administrator, I want rate limiting at the API Gateway so that excessive traffic cannot degrade ACD-07.
criteria: Apply configured consumer/tenant/scope limits; return HTTP 429 on excess traffic; rejected requests do not modify ACD-07 MongoDB; throttling metrics are available.

summary: As a Security Administrator, I want tenant isolation enforced on every API and query so that one organization cannot access another organization's calendars.
criteria: tenantId is mandatory for business records; ABAC restricts tenant/institution/campus/year; cross-tenant reads and writes are denied.

summary: As an API client, I want standardized pagination, filtering, sorting and error envelopes so that all ACD-07 APIs behave consistently.
criteria: All list APIs support standard pagination/filtering/sorting; domain errors map to documented HTTP status codes and codes.

summary: As an API client, I want retryable calendar writes to be idempotent so that network retries do not create duplicate data or publications.
criteria: Create/publish accepts Idempotency-Key; same key+same request returns stored outcome; same key+different hash is rejected; TTL applies where configured.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want calendar-domain events stored in an outbox with the business update so that downstream consumers receive reliable notifications.
criteria: Business state and outbox event commit atomically where practical; eventId is unique; payload/status/retry metadata are stored.

summary: As a downstream consumer, I want canonical ACD-07 events so that I can reliably react to calendar changes.
criteria: Published events include eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, entityType, entityId, version, correlationId and data.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want transient event-delivery failures retried so that temporary broker failures do not lose calendar notifications.
criteria: Retry transient failures using attemptCount/nextAttemptAt; retain delivery state until successful publication.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want poison events isolated in a dead-letter store so that repeated failures do not block healthy events.
criteria: After bounded retries, store event payload/failure reason/attempt count in dead_letter_events; support controlled replay and investigation.

summary: As an event consumer, I want duplicate events deduplicated by eventId so that retries do not cause duplicate downstream processing.
criteria: Consumer checks eventId, safely ignores already processed events, and retains correlation/causation identifiers.

summary: As the Academic Calendar Service, I want to consume CampusUpdated events so that calendar scope remains aligned with campus configuration.
criteria: Deduplicate by eventId; validate/refresh referenced campus context without owning campus data; failures are observable and handled through retry/DLQ.

summary: As the Academic Calendar Service, I want to consume InstitutionConfigurationChanged events so that calendar policies remain current.
criteria: Refresh/validate applicable working-day and publication policies; deduplicate; route failed processing through bounded retry/DLQ.

summary: As a downstream academic service, I want calendar changes distributed through APIs/events rather than database access so that ACD-07 remains the owner of calendar truth.
criteria: Consumers use stable calendarId/version/effective dates and event contracts; no downstream service can query academic_calendar_db directly.

summary: As a Management User, I want monthly, weekly, department and program-oriented calendar views so that I can review academic schedules.
criteria: Views derive from authoritative effective calendar; access is scoped; large report generation can run asynchronously.

summary: As a Management User, I want to export an authorized calendar to PDF, Excel or ICS so that schedule information can be shared through approved channels.
criteria: Export reflects effective or explicitly selected version; permissions are enforced; export is audited; large exports may be asynchronous.

summary: As a Management User, I want advisory calendar analytics so that I can identify instructional-day density, holiday concentration, term anomalies and change impact.
criteria: Analytics are derived from calendar data; insights are advisory only and cannot silently modify authoritative calendar state.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want current-calendar and date-range queries to use the defined MongoDB indexes so that ACD-07 meets its performance targets.
criteria: Verify indexes for current calendars, term dates, event dates/types and history; normal API P95 target <300ms and indexed search P95 <2s.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want ACD-07 to scale statelessly so that increasing campus/tenant load does not require service redesign.
criteria: Service pods remain stateless; indexes are tenant-aware; stable current-calendar reads may be safely cached; event streams can partition by tenant/institution.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want correlated logs, metrics and traces so that calendar workflow failures and delivery lag are diagnosable.
criteria: requestId/correlationId flow through API, persistence and event envelope; dashboards track API latency/errors, validation failures, publication latency, outbox lag, delivery failures, current-calendar count and upcoming events.

summary: As an API client, I want consistent ACD-07 domain errors so that I can handle failures safely.
criteria: Duplicate current=409; term overlap=422; invalid date=422; publish forbidden=403; version conflict=409; not found=404; dependency unavailable=503; deterministic validation failures are not retried.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want mandatory dependency failures to fail closed where policy validation is required so that invalid calendars are not published during dependency outages.
criteria: Required configuration/workflow/authorization dependencies produce controlled 503/failure; no unsafe publication occurs; failures are observable.

summary: As a System Administrator, I want retention policies applied to business and technical collections so that required records are preserved without uncontrolled technical growth.
criteria: Calendar history follows institutional retention; outbox retained through safe delivery plus safety window; DLQ through incident/audit period; idempotency records may use TTL.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want backup and restore verification so that recovery does not violate calendar integrity.
criteria: Encrypted backups/PITR where available; restore preserves versions/history and required outbox recovery; post-restore verification confirms exactly one current published calendar per required scope.

summary: As a System Administrator, I want MongoDB JSON Schema and application validation enforced so that invalid records cannot bypass domain rules.
criteria: Schemas validate required fields/types; compound unique indexes enforce business keys; reference and lifecycle validation occurs in application/domain layer; direct cross-service DB writes are prohibited.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want optimistic concurrency controls on calendar changes so that simultaneous administrators cannot silently overwrite each other.
criteria: Version fields are checked on updates/publication; stale expectedVersion produces ACD_CALENDAR_VERSION_CONFLICT 409; no partial state is committed.

summary: As a Development Team, I want approved OpenAPI, JSON Schema and event contracts for ACD-07 so that implementations and consumers remain compatible.
criteria: OpenAPI covers REST surface; JSON schemas validate MongoDB documents; event contracts are registered; contract tests cover REST and Event Bus compatibility.

summary: As a Development Team, I want automated tests for ACD-07 business and resilience rules so that releases do not break calendar integrity.
criteria: Unit tests cover dates/overlaps/lifecycle; integration tests cover MongoDB/workflow/config adapters; security tests cover RBAC/ABAC/tenant isolation; resilience tests cover DB/broker/dependency failures; E2E covers draft-to-consumer flow.

summary: As a Platform Operator, I want the ACD-07 production Definition of Done enforced so that the service is operationally ready.
criteria: OpenAPI approved; validators/indexes verified; publication transaction tested; outbox/idempotency/DLQ operational; workflow/RBAC reviewed; audit, dashboards, alerts, tracing, backup/restore and event contracts verified; tenant isolation passed.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want to register a learning resource with title, type, subject/course/curriculum context, so that the resource is available in the academic catalog.
criteria: Given I am an authorized faculty member, when I submit valid resource metadata, then ACD-08 creates a resource record and returns a resourceId, version and lifecycle status.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to register institutional learning resources, so that centrally managed academic content is cataloged.
criteria: The gateway authenticates and authorizes the administrator; valid metadata is persisted under the correct tenant/institution/campus.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want to associate a resource with a subject, course or curriculum, so that learners can find it in the correct academic context.
criteria: The service validates referenced academic identifiers and rejects missing or invalid references according to policy.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want to classify a resource by resource type, so that syllabi, study materials, links, videos and other content can be filtered correctly.
criteria: Only supported resource types are accepted and the selected type is stored in resources.resourceType.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want to add title, description and tags to a resource, so that users can understand and discover it.
criteria: Metadata is stored and tags are available to search/filter operations.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want to prevent duplicate business resource codes within a tenant, so that resource identity remains consistent.
criteria: A duplicate tenantId + resourceCode combination returns a conflict and does not create a second authoritative resource.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want to link a resource to binary content in shared object/document storage, so that ACD-08 manages metadata without owning binary bytes.
criteria: A valid immutable storageObjectRef/object reference is registered; binary content is not stored in MongoDB.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want to verify the object reference, MIME type, file size and checksum before publication, so that invalid content cannot become published academic content.
criteria: Invalid reference, unsupported MIME type, negative/invalid file size or invalid checksum prevents publication and produces the appropriate error.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want to create a new version of a resource instead of overwriting the existing version, so that previous academic content remains traceable.
criteria: A new version creates a new resource_versions record with a monotonic versionNo; no published version is overwritten.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to view resource version details, so that I can inspect file metadata, checksum and lifecycle state.
criteria: Authorized users can retrieve version metadata without exposing unauthorized storage references.

summary: As an authorized administrator, I want to restore an eligible previous version, so that an approved academic resource can be reverted without deleting its version history.
criteria: Restore creates or promotes an explicit version state according to lifecycle rules; existing immutable versions remain intact and the action is audited.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want optimistic version checks, so that concurrent updates do not silently overwrite resource state.
criteria: A stale expectedVersion results in ACD_RESOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT (409).

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to define who can view, download or manage a resource, so that institutional access policy is enforced.
criteria: A valid principal, scope, permission and effect are persisted as an access grant.

summary: As a Department Head, I want to manage resource access within my department, so that departmental governance rules are enforced.
criteria: The gateway and policy engine verify department scope before allowing access-policy changes.

summary: As an authorized administrator, I want to update an existing access rule, so that permissions remain current as academic responsibilities change.
criteria: The access rule is updated only within authorized scope and the change is audited.

summary: As an authorized administrator, I want to revoke resource access, so that users no longer retain permissions after the grant is withdrawn.
criteria: The grant changes to REVOKED with revokedBy/revokedAt recorded; subsequent authorization checks deny access when appropriate.

summary: As a Student, I want to view resources I am authorized to access, so that I can consume published academic materials.
criteria: Only published resources permitted by tenant/institution/department/course/subject/batch or explicit grants are returned.

summary: As a Student, I want to download a permitted resource using an authorized retrieval mechanism, so that binary content can be accessed securely.
criteria: ACD-08 verifies access before returning an authorized object reference or signed short-lived retrieval reference.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want deny rules to be evaluated according to institutional policy precedence, so that conflicting grants do not accidentally expose restricted content.
criteria: A request is denied when an applicable higher-precedence deny rule applies, and the denial is audited.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want a resource to begin in draft state, so that I can prepare and validate content before publication.
criteria: A newly registered resource enters the configured draft lifecycle state and is not treated as published content.

summary: As a Department Head, I want to approve a resource when departmental approval is configured, so that governance requirements are satisfied before publication.
criteria: Only an authorized approver can transition the resource through the configured review/approval state; approval reference is recorded.

summary: As an authorized publisher, I want to publish a validated resource version, so that it becomes available to permitted consumers.
criteria: Publication requires authorization, expectedVersion, ready access policy and valid immutable content reference; the published version becomes immutable.

summary: As an authorized governance user, I want to archive a published resource, so that obsolete content is removed from active catalogs without losing its history.
criteria: The resource transitions to archived state, the transition is audited, and LearningResourceArchived is emitted reliably.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want to prevent silent overwrite of published versions, so that academic records remain immutable and traceable.
criteria: Any attempt to modify a published version creates a new version or is rejected; the existing published version remains unchanged.

summary: As a Faculty member or Academic Admin, I want to publish a syllabus explicitly, so that the authoritative syllabus publication can be consumed by downstream services.
criteria: A valid syllabus publication creates the appropriate lifecycle record and emits SyllabusPublished with stable resource/version identifiers.

summary: As a Student, I want to search learning resources by subject, course and resource type, so that I can quickly find relevant academic material.
criteria: Search supports the documented filters and returns only resources permitted by the access policy.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want to search resources by title, tags and publication status, so that I can manage and reuse academic materials.
criteria: Search supports title/tags/status filters with standardized pagination, filtering and sorting.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve a resource by ID, so that I can inspect its authoritative metadata and current lifecycle state.
criteria: The service returns the resource metadata when authorized and returns ACD_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown resource.

summary: As an authorized user, I want to retrieve available tags, so that I can use consistent metadata for catalog filtering.
criteria: The service returns tags within the caller's authorized tenant/scope.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want indexed resource queries, so that catalog search meets the documented performance target.
criteria: Normal indexed search operations use the planned MongoDB/search indexes and support the target search P95 of less than 2 seconds.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want every resource lifecycle transition recorded, so that academic content changes are traceable.
criteria: Create, version, publish, syllabus publication, archive and relevant access-policy changes are recorded with actor, time, old/new state and correlationId.

summary: As an authorized auditor, I want to inspect resource history, so that I can trace how a resource and its versions changed over time.
criteria: History is append-only and can be queried by resource and timestamp without destructive modification.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want access failures and administrative changes audited, so that unauthorized or exceptional activity is traceable.
criteria: Policy denials, access failures, administrative changes and export/access failures generate audit records with actor, scope and correlationId.

summary: As an LMS/Search/Analytics/CAM consumer, I want to receive LearningResourceCreated events, so that I can update downstream resource views without querying ACD-08's database directly.
criteria: A LearningResourceCreated event contains eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, entityType, entityId, version, correlationId and data.

summary: As a downstream consumer, I want LearningResourcePublished events, so that I can make newly published resources available in downstream catalogs.
criteria: Publication generates one reliable event representing the published resource/version.

summary: As a downstream consumer, I want LearningResourceArchived events, so that archived resources are removed from active downstream catalogs.
criteria: Archive commits the lifecycle change and produces a reliable archive event.

summary: As a downstream consumer, I want SyllabusPublished events, so that syllabus publication can be synchronized across academic services.
criteria: A syllabus publication event identifies the authoritative resource and version and is delivered reliably.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want to consume SubjectCreated and CurriculumPublished events, so that resource references remain aligned with academic context.
criteria: Consumed events are processed idempotently and their context is available for catalog/reference validation.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want transactional outbox records created with resource lifecycle changes, so that events are not lost after a successful database commit.
criteria: Business state and outbox state are committed atomically where practical; unpublished outbox events are retryable.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want retryable writes protected by idempotency keys, so that repeated requests do not create duplicate resources or transitions.
criteria: The same tenantId + idempotencyKey with the same request hash returns the stored response; a different hash is rejected.

summary: As a system operator, I want failed events moved to a dead-letter store after exhausted retries, so that poison events can be investigated and replayed safely.
criteria: Exhausted event failures are recorded with eventId, reason, attemptCount and replayCount without losing the original payload.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want transient storage and broker failures retried with bounded backoff, so that temporary infrastructure failures recover automatically.
criteria: Transient failures are retried; deterministic validation and authorization failures are not retried.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to export authorized resource metadata, so that I can support institutional reporting and catalog administration.
criteria: Export contains only authorized metadata and respects tenant/scope policy; long-running exports are asynchronous.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want resource usage analytics, so that I can understand access demand and identify stale or highly used resources.
criteria: Usage data is exposed through the configured analytics endpoint/service without changing resource lifecycle automatically.

summary: As a system operator, I want tenant, institution and campus isolation enforced on every resource operation, so that one academic tenant cannot access another tenant's data.
criteria: Queries and mutations require tenant context and cross-tenant access is denied and audited.

summary: As a system operator, I want direct database sharing with other services prohibited, so that ACD-08 remains the authoritative boundary for resource metadata and access policy.
criteria: Downstream services consume APIs/events rather than directly querying academic_resource_db.

summary: As a system operator, I want resource registration, publication latency, search P95, policy denials, version creation, outbox lag and DLQ depth measured, so that service health can be monitored.
criteria: The service exposes/records the documented operational metrics and distributed traces across Gateway, ACD-08, MongoDB, object storage, outbox and broker.

summary: As a system operator, I want resource metadata, versions, access policy and history backed up and restored consistently with object references, so that academic resources remain recoverable.
criteria: Restore tests verify metadata and object references remain consistent; object storage has its own versioning/replication/backup policy.
