summary: As a Faculty member, I want ownership of a resource validated against my academic scope, so that I cannot register resources outside my authorized department, subject, course or tenant.
criteria: The service validates tenant/institution/campus and ownership context before registration; unauthorized ownership returns an authorization error and is audited.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want registration metadata validated for supported resource type, MIME type, file size and checksum rules, so that invalid resource records cannot enter the lifecycle.
criteria: Unsupported resource types/MIME types, invalid file size or malformed checksum are rejected with deterministic validation errors; no invalid resource/version record is committed.

summary: As a Student, I want a short-lived authorized retrieval reference for permitted content, so that binary content can be downloaded without exposing permanent storage credentials.
criteria: Authorization is evaluated before a retrieval reference is returned; the reference is short-lived and scoped to the permitted object/version; unauthorized users receive a policy denial.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want access grants to support time windows, so that permissions automatically apply only during their valid period.
criteria: validFrom/validTo are validated; expired grants are not treated as active; invalid date windows are rejected; grant changes are audited.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want access grants validated for conflicts and policy precedence, so that contradictory permissions do not create unintended access.
criteria: Conflicting grants are detected according to institutional policy; deny precedence is respected; invalid combinations are rejected or resolved according to configured policy and audited.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want each access-policy change associated with a policy version, so that authorization decisions remain traceable and reproducible.
criteria: Every access-policy mutation records policyVersion; authorization/audit records can identify the policy version applicable to the grant.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want to scope a resource to an academic batch or program where permitted, so that access reflects the intended learner population.
criteria: Batch/program scope is represented in the authorization context where configured; users outside the permitted scope cannot retrieve the resource.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want duplicate content detected using checksum/contentHash, so that accidental duplicate resource versions can be identified.
criteria: The service can detect matching checksum/contentHash values within the applicable tenant/resource scope and surface the duplicate condition without overwriting existing content.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want resource lifecycle changes synchronized with the search index, so that search results reflect current publication and archive state.
criteria: Create/publish/archive changes generate the integration signal needed by the search service; stale indexed records are reconciled without direct database sharing.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want to bulk import resource metadata and references, so that large academic catalogs can be onboarded efficiently.
criteria: Bulk import validates each record, isolates invalid records according to the configured import policy, is asynchronous for long-running jobs, and preserves idempotency and auditability.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want export jobs to have a trackable lifecycle, so that large exports can be submitted, monitored and retrieved without blocking the API.
criteria: The export request returns a job reference; status can be checked; completion produces an authorized result; failures are traceable and do not expose unauthorized records.

summary: As an ACD-08 event consumer, I want duplicate events detected by eventId, so that retries do not create duplicate downstream actions.
criteria: A previously processed eventId is recognized and not processed as a new business event; processing remains traceable through correlation/causation identifiers.

summary: As a system operator, I want dead-letter events replayed after remediation, so that recoverable failed events can be reprocessed without losing their original context.
criteria: An authorized operator can replay an eligible DLQ event; replayCount and outcome are recorded; replay does not bypass idempotency or authorization controls.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want retention rules applied to drafts, versions, access records and history, so that records follow institutional academic governance requirements.
criteria: Retention categories are configurable according to institutional policy; published syllabus/resource history is retained as required; draft operational data can follow shorter retention without deleting required academic records.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want stale-resource and resource-demand insights, so that I can identify resources that may need review or improved coverage.
criteria: Analytics can surface usage trends, stale-resource signals, syllabus coverage, resource-type distribution and access-demand patterns; insights are advisory and cannot silently change lifecycle state.

summary: As the ACD-08 service, I want resource context validated against the academic calendar where applicable, so that resources can be aligned with the relevant academic period.
criteria: When academic-period context is required by the resource policy, the service validates the referenced academic period and rejects or quarantines invalid context according to policy.

summary: As a system operator, I want disaster-recovery tests to verify metadata-to-object-reference consistency, so that restored resources do not point to missing or incompatible binary content.
criteria: Recovery tests validate resources, versions, access policies and history against object-storage references; inconsistencies are detected before restored content is exposed.

summary: Create an assessment structure for a subject so the institution has an authoritative assessment definition.
criteria: Valid subject/context creates DRAFT; duplicate business identity returns 409.

summary: Create an assessment structure within assigned subject scope.
criteria: Gateway and ABAC enforce tenant/institution/department/subject scope.

summary: Prevent duplicate assessment identity within a tenant and academic context.
criteria: Unique tenant+assessmentCode+academicYear+subjectId is enforced.

summary: Configure internal, external, practical and other supported assessment types.
criteria: Unsupported assessment types are rejected.

summary: Associate an assessment with subject, course, curriculum, term and academic year where applicable.
criteria: References and mandatory academic context are validated.

summary: Update a draft assessment structure before approval.
criteria: Authorized draft changes are audited; published structures cannot be edited in place.

summary: Add tests, assignments, practicals, exams and other components.
criteria: Component is linked to a valid assessment and passes type/marks validation.

summary: Configure maximum marks for each component.
criteria: Marks are valid and satisfy component policy.

summary: Configure component weightage.
criteria: Weightage is validated against assessment rules.

summary: Configure passing marks.
criteria: passingMarks cannot exceed maximumMarks.

summary: Configure component sequence/order.
criteria: assessmentId+sequenceNo is unique.

summary: Configure rubric, evaluation method and attempt policy.
criteria: Configured evaluation metadata is validated and stored.

summary: Retrieve components for an assessment.
criteria: Authorized users receive sequence, marks, weightage and evaluation configuration.

summary: Update a draft component.
criteria: Only authorized draft components change; stale versions return 409.

summary: Delete an invalid draft component.
criteria: Deletion is allowed only under lifecycle rules; published components remain immutable.

summary: Reconcile component weightage with configured assessment total.
criteria: Validation returns deterministic weight mismatch diagnostics.

summary: Reconcile maximum-mark totals.
criteria: Component maximum marks are compared with configured totalMarks.

summary: Validate passing-mark constraints.
criteria: Invalid passingMarks/maximumMarks relationships are rejected.

summary: Validate an assessment before submission.
criteria: Validation identifies weightage, marks, uniqueness, subject and outcome errors.

summary: Map a component to CO, PO or learning outcome.
criteria: Referenced outcome is valid and unique mapping is created.

summary: Support component-level and assessment-level mappings.
criteria: Only supported mappingLevel values are accepted.

summary: Assign mapping weight to an outcome relationship.
criteria: Mapping weight is within configured range.

summary: Configure attainment policy reference for an outcome mapping.
criteria: Configured attainment policy reference is validated and retained.

summary: Prevent duplicate outcome mappings.
criteria: Unique assessment+component+outcome combination is enforced.

summary: Retrieve assessment outcome mappings.
criteria: Authorized queries return mappings by assessment/component/outcome type.

summary: Retrieve the effective assessment map for a subject.
criteria: Returns authorized effective published mapping for the academic context.

summary: Retrieve approved assessment context for examination execution.
criteria: Only approved/published context is exposed; EXM cannot modify ACD-09 data.

summary: Manage Draft→Review→Approved→Published→Retired lifecycle.
criteria: Only configured transitions are allowed; rejected/cancelled draft outcomes are terminal.

summary: Review and approve departmental assessment structures.
criteria: Department scope and approval context are enforced and audited.

summary: Publish a validated assessment mapping.
criteria: Authorization, expectedVersion, approval and validation succeed before atomic publication; immutable version and outbox record are created.

summary: Keep published assessment definitions immutable.
criteria: Changes to published structures/mappings require a new version.

summary: Prevent concurrent edits from silently overwriting assessment definitions.
criteria: Stale expectedVersion returns ACD_ASSESSMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT.

summary: View assessment version history.
criteria: History includes version, action, transition, actor, reason and approval reference.

summary: Audit component, mapping, approval, publication and retirement changes.
criteria: History captures old/new state, actor, timestamp, reason, approval and correlationId.

summary: Audit authorization failures.
criteria: Protected API failures record actor, scope, time and correlationId.

summary: Receive AssessmentStructureCreated events.
criteria: Canonical event envelope is emitted reliably after creation.

summary: Receive AssessmentMappingUpdated events.
criteria: Draft mapping changes produce reliable versioned events.

summary: Receive AssessmentMappingPublished events.
criteria: Published event is emitted only after successful commit and identifies effective version.

summary: Consume SubjectPublished events.
criteria: Subject context is validated/activated idempotently; mandatory dependency failure fails closed.

summary: Consume CurriculumPublished events.
criteria: Affected assessment structures can be identified and marked review-needed; published definitions are not mutated.

summary: Consume CourseUpdated events.
criteria: Affected assessment structures are identified and course context refreshed without modifying course ownership.

summary: Commit business changes and outbox records atomically where practical.
criteria: No successful authoritative change can lose its corresponding event record.

summary: Protect retryable writes with Idempotency-Key.
criteria: Same key+request hash returns stored result; different hash is rejected.

summary: Retry transient broker failures with bounded backoff.
criteria: Transient failures retry; deterministic validation/authorization failures do not.

summary: Store poison events in a dead-letter collection.
criteria: DLQ retains event identity, payload, failure details, attempts and replay count.

summary: Replay remediated dead-letter events safely.
criteria: Replay is authorized, replayCount updates, original identity is preserved and eventId idempotency prevents duplicate business effects.

summary: Enforce tenant, institution, department, subject and course scope.
criteria: Out-of-scope access is denied before data is returned or changed and is audited.

summary: Provide read-only approved assessment context to EXM.
criteria: EXM can read published context but cannot modify ACD-09-owned data.

summary: Prevent direct database sharing with EXM, LMS and Analytics.
criteria: Consumers use APIs/events and cannot write ACD-09 collections directly.

summary: View assessment coverage and mapping completeness analytics.
criteria: Reports cover component distribution, outcome coverage, program-wise plans and unmapped outcomes without changing authoritative data.

summary: View assessment-load and balance insights.
criteria: Advisory analytics cover load distribution, weightage patterns, rubric complexity and balance.

summary: Export authorized assessment structures and mappings.
criteria: Exports respect authorization and are asynchronous for long-running operations.

summary: Query assessments by subject, course, term and academic year.
criteria: Queries use tenant-aware indexes and support filtering/pagination.

summary: Ensure only one effective published version exists for an assessment context.
criteria: Publication prevents conflicting effective versions and handles publication races with 409.

summary: Retire an obsolete assessment mapping.
criteria: Retirement is authorized, audited and retains historical versions.

summary: Identify assessments affected by curriculum changes.
criteria: CurriculumPublished identifies affected structures and policy can mark them review-needed without mutating published definitions.

summary: Review assessment definitions affected by course/curriculum changes.
criteria: Affected structures expose current effective version and review status; published history remains unchanged.

summary: Validate subject, course, curriculum and outcome references.
criteria: Invalid references are rejected or fail closed according to dependency policy.

summary: Keep assessment reads within documented performance targets.
criteria: Normal API P95 targets <300ms and indexed search/mapping P95 targets <2s under baseline.

summary: Monitor creation rate, validation failures, publication latency, weightage conflicts, API P95, outbox lag, event failures and consumer lag.
criteria: Documented metrics and Gateway→ACD-09→MongoDB→outbox→broker traces are available.

summary: Perform encrypted backups and restore drills.
criteria: Restore validation confirms preserved history, tenant isolation and no conflicting effective versions.

summary: Apply institutional retention to published definitions, mappings and history.
criteria: Published academic records follow institutional retention; draft/technical records may use shorter operational windows.

summary: Perform institutional assessment administration within authorized scope.
criteria: Create, update, map, approve, publish, retire, report and audit actions require proper role and scope.

summary: Review and approve departmental assessment structures.
criteria: Department scope is enforced and approvalRef records approval context.

summary: Provide standardized API envelopes, errors, pagination, filtering, sorting and correlation metadata.
criteria: All APIs use /api/v1 conventions and documented ACD-09 error codes.

summary: Protect assessment definitions and confidential approval/history data.
criteria: TLS, encryption at rest, least privilege, tenant isolation and scoped exports are enforced.

summary: Receive approved assessment context without owning assessment definitions.
criteria: LMS receives authorized published context through APIs/events and cannot directly modify ACD-09 data.

summary: Detect required-but-missing component-to-outcome mappings.
criteria: Validation blocks publication when policy requires complete outcome mapping.

summary: Reuse assessment templates to create new draft structures.
criteria: Template reuse creates a new draft while retaining scope, validation and lifecycle controls.

summary: Support multi-program and multi-department assessment contexts where configured.
criteria: Program/department context is subject to ABAC and cannot bypass scope controls.

summary: As an authenticated user, I want ACD-10 APIs routed through the API Gateway so that requests receive centralized authentication, routing, and rate limiting.
criteria: Given a request to an ACD-10 route, when it reaches the gateway, then the gateway validates the configured authentication token, applies routing and rate limits, and forwards only permitted requests; unauthenticated requests return 401 and rate-limited requests return 429.

summary: As the service, I want authentication and authorization enforced at both the gateway and service boundary so that gateway bypass cannot expose analytics.
criteria: Requests without valid identity are rejected; ACD-10 independently validates caller identity and authorization; service-to-service identities use least privilege; security decisions are logged where required.

summary: As a tenant administrator, I want every analytics query and stored record scoped to my institution so that data cannot leak across tenants.
criteria: Every business and technical record includes tenantId; repository queries derive tenant scope from trusted identity; client-supplied tenantId cannot override authorized context; cross-tenant access requires an explicitly privileged reporting context; tests prove isolation.

summary: As an Academic Admin, I want institution-wide dashboards and policy-controlled exports so that I can monitor academic performance within my permitted scope.
criteria: Institution scope is permitted only for authorized Academic Admins; restricted metrics are separately authorized; export permissions are policy-checked; denied decisions return 403 and are audited.

summary: As a Department Head, I want analytics limited to my department so that I can review department, batch, subject, and faculty performance without seeing unrelated departments.
criteria: Department scope is resolved from trusted role assignments; requested scopeId is checked against that assignment; cross-department requests return 403; permitted results contain only authorized scope data.

summary: As a Faculty member, I want analytics for my assigned subjects and batches so that I can monitor attendance and academic progress within my teaching responsibilities.
criteria: Only assigned scopes are returned; unassigned batch/subject IDs are denied; restricted individual-level metrics require additional policy authorization; access decisions are auditable.

summary: As an authorized Student or Parent, I want only policy-permitted personal or published academic analytics so that I can view relevant information without accessing other people's records.
criteria: Student scope is limited to self; Parent scope is limited to an explicitly authorized student; unpublished or restricted metrics are withheld; exports remain restricted unless policy explicitly allows them.

summary: As a user requesting sensitive analytics, I want metric classification and scope-based authorization applied so that confidential and restricted data is disclosed only when permitted.
criteria: Metrics carry or inherit a defined classification; PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, and RESTRICTED controls are applied; unauthorized access returns 403; sensitive queries are logged according to policy.

summary: As an API consumer, I want validated date ranges, filters, deterministic sorting, and bounded query limits so that analytics requests are predictable and safe.
criteria: Invalid dates, reversed ranges, unsupported filters, excessive ranges, or invalid sort keys return 400; maximum ranges and row limits are configurable; list results use deterministic sorting; production dashboard paths use indexed projections.

summary: As an API consumer, I want consistent versioned API responses and actionable errors so that clients can handle failures reliably.
criteria: The five canonical endpoints are versioned; errors include code, message, and correlationId; documented cases map to 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500, or 503 as applicable; internal diagnostics are not leaked.

summary: As an authorized user, I want a role-filtered academic dashboard so that I can see current KPIs for my permitted organizational scope.
criteria: GET dashboard accepts period and scope; response includes only authorized scope metrics; includes attendance, timetable utilization, active course/batch measures where available; response includes asOf and projectionLagSeconds or equivalent freshness metadata.

summary: As a Management user, I want institution-approved executive and aggregated trends so that I can review academic performance without unnecessary individual-level data.
criteria: Management views return only authorized executive/aggregated metrics; individual-level restricted data is excluded; filters cannot widen the user's authorized scope; freshness is shown.

summary: As an authorized academic user, I want attendance analytics by batch, subject, faculty, and date range so that I can identify attendance patterns.
criteria: Endpoint filters by authorized batch and date range; response groups counts by subject and includes present, absent, and percentage values; totals and percentages follow the approved denominator definition; freshness is returned.

summary: As an authorized user, I want attendance shortage risk signals alongside attendance summaries so that I can identify batches or subjects requiring follow-up.
criteria: Configured shortage threshold is applied to sufficiently fresh metrics; risk level is stored with the projection; stale metrics do not trigger a new risk alert; repeated unchanged risk states do not create alert storms.

summary: As an authorized user, I want timetable utilization by room, faculty, batch, and slot type so that I can understand use of scheduled academic resources.
criteria: Endpoint supports date range and department scope; response includes scheduled, executed, and cancelled slot counts and utilization; configured policy defines denominator treatment for cancelled, substituted, or rescheduled sessions; unauthorized scopes are denied.

summary: As a permitted user, I want underutilized rooms and faculty/resource summaries so that I can investigate utilization patterns.
criteria: Results are grouped by permitted scope; underutilization thresholds are configurable; response identifies resource type, reference, and utilization; missing or stale projections are identified rather than silently treated as zero.

summary: As an authorized user, I want course, curriculum, and assessment coverage analytics so that I can track academic progression against approved plans.
criteria: Endpoint supports batch and academic period; response includes course completion, curriculum coverage, assessment coverage, and period trend where data exists; calculations use approved upstream events and do not invent unsupported completion facts.

summary: As an authorized user, I want progression risk indicators based on configured targets so that I can identify courses or batches falling behind.
criteria: Configured period targets and deterministic rule versions are applied; risk level and asOf are persisted; only supported facts contribute; threshold crossings or risk-state transitions generate the appropriate insight event.

summary: As an authorized analytics user, I want approved role/group engagement aggregates so that I can understand report or dashboard consumption without collecting unnecessary personal behavior.
criteria: Only explicitly approved metric types are stored; records are aggregated by audienceType, scopeRef, metricType, and periodKey; raw personal behavior is not stored unless policy requires it; classification and scope checks are enforced.

summary: As an authorized report designer, I want reusable report definitions and approved templates so that users can generate consistent standard or custom reports.
criteria: A definition includes a stable identifier, name, code, description, type, parameters, system flag, creator, and timestamps; required parameters and allowed filters are validated; only authorized roles can create or update custom definitions.

summary: As the event consumer, I want to consume supported academic domain events from the event bus so that analytics projections remain decoupled from operational services.
criteria: Consumer supports CourseCreated, CurriculumPublished, BatchCreated, TimetablePublished, AttendanceMarked, AcademicCalendarPublished, and AssessmentMappingPublished; it validates event envelopes and tenant context; it does not query upstream operational databases.

summary: As the analytics pipeline, I want heterogeneous source events normalized into canonical analytical facts so that metrics can be calculated consistently across services.
criteria: Each accepted fact stores tenantId, sourceEventId/type/service, entity type/id, occurredAt, processedAt, factType, schemaVersion, and classification; applicable subject/course/batch/faculty/term references and dimensions/measures are populated; source ownership remains upstream.

summary: As the event consumer, I want duplicate event delivery to be idempotent so that retries do not inflate counts or duplicate facts.
criteria: Uniqueness of tenantId plus sourceEventId is enforced; duplicate deliveries do not change aggregate totals twice; processing outcome is recorded using idempotency controls; concurrent duplicate deliveries are safely handled.

summary: As the event consumer, I want late and out-of-order events handled through targeted recomputation so that analytical projections remain accurate.
criteria: Events inside the configured recomputation window are accepted; affected aggregates are recomputed rather than destructively overwritten; projection versions increase monotonically; events outside policy are quarantined or handled according to documented retention/reconciliation rules.

summary: As an operator, I want malformed or non-retryable events quarantined with diagnostics so that poison messages do not block unrelated processing.
criteria: Invalid envelopes and schema/business failures are sent to the dead-letter collection with event identity, source, payload, failure code/message, attempt count, and timestamps; raw payload is not exposed to ordinary business users; unrelated partitions continue processing.

summary: As an operator, I want authorized replay of dead-letter events so that recoverable failures can be corrected without duplicating analytics.
criteria: Replay requires a privileged role and an audit record; replay status changes are tracked; original event identity is preserved; replay is idempotent; events can be marked replayed or abandoned with reason.

summary: As an operator, I want event consumer lag and processing failures monitored so that stale analytics and pipeline incidents can be detected.
criteria: Metrics expose consumer lag, processed/failed counts, throughput, and projection freshness; alerts can be configured against operational SLAs; logs include eventId, correlationId, tenantId, duration, and projectionVersion without leaking sensitive payloads.

summary: As an operator, I want source event schemas and versions validated so that incompatible event changes do not silently corrupt analytics.
criteria: Each event envelope has required eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, version, correlationId, tenant context, and applicable causationId; unsupported schema versions are rejected or quarantined; compatible changes are contract-tested.

summary: As the projection engine, I want attendance aggregates updated from normalized facts so that attendance queries are fast and consistent.
criteria: Projection keys include tenant, period, batch, subject, faculty, and date bucket as applicable; counters cannot be negative; percentage is between 0 and 100; unique aggregate keys prevent duplicate projection documents; projection version and freshness are updated.

summary: As the projection engine, I want academic progression aggregates updated from course, curriculum, batch, and assessment events so that coverage trends are available.
criteria: Projection stores period and applicable course/subject/batch/curriculum/assessment references; completion and coverage values are derived only from supported facts; unique aggregate keys and indexes support common queries; version increments monotonically.

summary: As the projection engine, I want timetable utilization aggregates updated from timetable and calendar events so that utilization can be queried without scanning raw events.
criteria: Projection supports period, batch, room, faculty, and slot type dimensions; scheduled/executed/cancelled counts are non-negative; utilization follows configured business definition; freshness and version are recorded.

summary: As an operator, I want projections rebuilt from retained events or an approved data pipeline so that corrupted or stale read models can be recovered.
criteria: Rebuild runs in an isolated staging projection or versioned rebuild; event replay does not corrupt live reads; record counts and metric invariants are validated; cutover occurs only after validation; rebuild operation is audited.

summary: As an operator, I want projection freshness and version metadata exposed so that users and support teams can distinguish delayed analytics from missing data.
criteria: Each projection exposes asOf, updatedAt, and projectionVersion; dashboard responses expose freshness or lag; stale-projection SLA violations are observable; caches invalidate or expire when projection version changes.

summary: As an operator, I want projection updates and corresponding output-event records committed atomically where supported so that downstream consumers are not notified of uncommitted metrics.
criteria: Projection changes and associated outbox record are committed in one MongoDB transaction where transaction boundaries are appropriate; cross-service transactions are not used; failed transactions leave neither a partial projection update nor an orphan event.

summary: As an authorized administrator, I want KPI and risk thresholds configurable by institution, academic year, or policy so that calculations reflect approved institutional rules.
criteria: Rules are versioned; threshold changes are authorized and auditable; calculation output records the rule/version where required; deterministic baseline calculations can be reproduced.

summary: As a downstream consumer, I want AcademicMetricCalculated events published when approved metrics are recalculated so that BI and intelligence services can consume governed metrics.
criteria: Event contains eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, tenantId, version, correlationId, entity identity, and metric data; event is published through the outbox after commit; consumers can deduplicate it.

summary: As a downstream notification consumer, I want AttendanceRiskDetected events only when a risk state transitions into an alert condition so that users are not flooded with duplicate alerts.
criteria: Event is emitted when configured threshold and freshness checks pass and risk state transitions; deduplication window suppresses repeated unchanged states; event includes tenant/scope and correlation metadata.

summary: As a downstream BI consumer, I want TimetableUtilizationCalculated events published after utilization recalculation so that resource analytics can be integrated without querying ACD-10 MongoDB.
criteria: Event contains metric scope, value/measures, freshness, tenant and correlation metadata; it is reliably published through outbox; consumers use the event/data feed rather than direct database access.

summary: As an intelligence consumer, I want validated AcademicInsightGenerated events so that higher-level intelligence services can consume governed insights.
criteria: Insight is generated from approved facts and versioned rules; required event envelope fields are present; publication is reliable and deduplicable; only authorized/approved insight content is published.

summary: As an authorized user, I want to request a report export with a report type, format, and filters so that I can obtain a controlled copy of analytical results.
criteria: POST export validates report type, format, filter schema, tenant, scope, date range, and row limits; request is authorized before job creation; large exports return 202 with jobId, QUEUED status, and poll URI; repeated command with same idempotency key does not create duplicate jobs.

summary: As the export worker, I want report jobs processed asynchronously from indexed projections so that large reports do not block interactive APIs.
criteria: Job progresses through REQUESTED/QUEUED/RUNNING to COMPLETED or FAILED/EXPIRED; worker uses indexed projections and bounded filters; retries are controlled; job status and timing are persisted; interactive APIs return promptly.

summary: As an export worker, I want sensitive fields filtered according to the caller's policy so that generated files do not disclose unauthorized data.
criteria: Authorization and field-level policy are re-evaluated at job execution or a documented authorization snapshot is used; output contains only allowed fields and scopes; unauthorized jobs fail safely and are audited.

summary: As a report requester, I want to check the status of my export job so that I know whether the report is queued, running, complete, failed, or expired.
criteria: Status lookup verifies tenant and requester/role scope; unknown or unauthorized job access does not disclose job details; response includes status, timestamps, and permitted error information; completed jobs expose a controlled output reference and expiry.

summary: As a report requester, I want completed exports delivered through controlled, expiring object-storage references so that files are not stored indefinitely in MongoDB or exposed publicly.
criteria: Binary artifacts are stored outside MongoDB; access is authorized and audited; expiry is enforced; expired links/files are inaccessible; output references are tenant-bound and not guessable.

summary: As an auditor, I want export requests, authorization decisions, completions, downloads, and failures recorded so that report access is traceable.
criteria: Audit entries capture requester, tenant, scope, report type, filters or safe filter summary, decision, timestamps, correlationId, result, and artifact expiry; audit is append-only and access-controlled; secrets and unnecessary sensitive values are excluded.

summary: As an operator, I want failed export jobs to retain a safe diagnostic and support controlled retry so that transient failures can be recovered.
criteria: Failure marks the job FAILED with a normalized error code and safe diagnostic; retries follow bounded policy; repeated retries do not create duplicate artifacts; retry and final outcome are auditable.

summary: As a report requester, I want to export supported reports in approved formats such as PDF, XLSX, and CSV so that I can use the results in institutional workflows.
criteria: Only configured formats are accepted; unsupported formats return 400; file content matches selected filters and authorized scope; generated file metadata records format, size/type where available, creation and expiry.

summary: As the event publisher, I want publication intent persisted in an outbox with metric changes so that committed analytics events are not lost.
criteria: Outbox records contain unique eventId, tenantId, eventType, aggregate identity, payload, status, attempt count, and timestamps; publication is retried; successful publication records publishedAt; unique eventId is enforced.

summary: As an operator, I want failed outbox publications retried with bounded backoff so that temporary event-bus failures recover without manual data repair.
criteria: Pending/failed records are retried according to nextAttemptAt and bounded exponential backoff with jitter; attemptCount increments; permanently failed items are observable and handled by policy; duplicate downstream delivery is safe.

summary: As a client or event consumer, I want idempotency records to protect repeated commands and event deliveries so that retries do not duplicate effects.
criteria: Record key includes tenantId, idempotencyKey, and operation; requestHash detects key reuse with a different payload; status transitions are controlled; completed responses can be referenced; expiry follows configured retention policy and TTL behavior.

summary: As an operator, I want failed events stored with normalized diagnostics and replay status so that failures can be investigated and resolved.
criteria: DLQ record preserves tenantId, eventId/type, source service, payload, failure code/message, attempt count, first/last failure times, replayStatus, and createdAt; unique tenant/event key prevents duplicate DLQ records; replay history is auditable.

summary: As the service, I want MongoDB schemas and indexes to enforce analytical data integrity so that invalid or duplicate data cannot corrupt reports.
criteria: Required fields and types are validated; tenantId and schemaVersion are present where required; IDs are immutable; counters are non-negative; percentages stay within defined bounds; compound unique indexes enforce aggregate keys; indexes support documented query patterns.

summary: As a data-governance operator, I want retention and archival policies applied by data class and institution so that analytics data is retained only as long as approved.
criteria: Retention periods are configurable rather than hard-coded; idempotency TTL follows policy; facts can be archived to an approved data-lake tier; DLQ records remain until resolved/closed and then archived; export artifacts expire according to policy.

summary: As a platform operator, I want recoverable backups and a documented restore sequence so that analytics can be restored after data loss or infrastructure failure.
criteria: Backups and point-in-time recovery are configured where supported; recovery restores MongoDB and event processing in documented order; offsets and projection versions are reconciled; critical exports can be regenerated; recovery is tested.

summary: As a dashboard user, I want common dashboard reads served from indexed projections and appropriately scoped caches so that responses remain fast without exposing stale or cross-tenant data.
criteria: Dashboard paths do not scan raw facts; normal indexed API P95 target is below 300 ms and indexed analytical query P95 below 2 seconds under agreed test conditions; cache keys include tenant and authorization scope; projection version/asOf informs invalidation; sensitive metrics are not cached unrestricted.

summary: As an operator, I want service, database, export, and projection health metrics so that reliability and performance issues can be diagnosed.
criteria: Telemetry includes dashboard P95, MongoDB query latency, export queue depth/failure rate, consumer lag, events processed/failed, rebuild duration, projection freshness, and risk-event counts; logs correlate operations with correlationId and tenant context while protecting sensitive data.

summary: As a user, I want analytics failures to degrade safely without blocking operational academic transactions so that core academic workflows continue when ACD-10 is unavailable.
criteria: Upstream services do not synchronously depend on ACD-10; dashboard/query outages return controlled errors; event ingestion retries or buffers according to policy; recovery catches up from retained events; service availability target is measured against the agreed 99.9% objective.

summary: As a downstream BI or intelligence consumer, I want governed metrics and published events/data feeds so that I can consume analytics without querying ACD-10's MongoDB directly.
criteria: Approved consumers receive documented event/data contracts; events include tenant, version, scope, metric and correlation metadata; access is authenticated and authorized; no downstream consumer is granted direct operational access to ACD-10 MongoDB.

summary: As a QA engineer, I want unit, repository, contract, integration, replay, performance, security, data-quality, and disaster-recovery tests so that ACD-10 meets its production acceptance criteria.
criteria: Tests cover deterministic calculations, thresholds, validators, tenant isolation, indexes, REST/event contracts, MongoDB plus event bus/outbox, duplicate/late/out-of-order replay, dashboard P95, export authorization, restore, count reconciliation, and metric invariants; release is blocked on critical failures.

summary: As an API platform owner, I want the architecture-image route families mapped to the detailed-design canonical endpoints so that clients use a consistent, documented contract.
criteria: A route map documents /api/v1/reports, /api/v1/dashboards, /api/v1/kpis, /api/v1/analytics/attendance, /performance, /enrolment, /exports, and /schedules against canonical ACD-10 routes or explicitly approved separate APIs; unsupported routes are not exposed; OpenAPI and gateway configuration agree.
